rashi.eng: *for perfumers.* who prepare perfumes and spices for women’s cosmetics.

notes.207: (tn): Or “eunuchs” (so NAB); NIV “officials”; KJV, NASB, NRSV, NLT “officers.”

notes.208: (tc): The LXX adds “because you have chosen for yourselves a king.”

notes.209: (tn, Heb): “and the people refused to listen to the voice of Samuel.”

notes.211: (tn, Heb): “and Samuel heard all the words of the people and he spoke them into the ears of the Lord.”

notes.215: (tc): The Syriac Peshitta includes the following words: “So Saul arose and went out. He took with him one of the boys and went out to look for his father’s donkeys.”

notes.216: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Saul) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*בארץ צוף.* 
בארעא דבה נביא:
rashi.eng: *into the land of Zuph.* (Jonathan renders:) into the land wherein there was a prophet.

rashi.heb:
*צוף.* 
כמו 'צופה':
rashi.eng: *Zuph.* like ‘Zopheh,’ a prophet (or seer).

rashi.heb:
*פן יחדל אבי מן האתונות.* 
שתגדל דאגה שלנו עליו, עד שישכח את האתונות:
rashi.eng: *lest my father cease to worry about the she-asses.* because his worry for us will increase until he forgets the she-asses.

rashi.heb:
*ודאג.* 
איטוביטאר"ה בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *and worry.* doutera in French.

notes.217: (tn): The infinitive absolute precedes the verb for emphasis.
notes.218: (tn, Heb): “our way on which we have gone.”

rashi.heb:
*את דרכנו.* 
מעשה האתונות מה נהיתה בם, שבשבילם הלכנו את כל הדרך הזה:
rashi.eng: *our way.* The story of the she-asses, i.e., what has become of them, for whom we have gone all this way.

rashi.heb:
*ומה נביא לאיש.* 
תרגם יונתן: אם מקבל ממון, מה נעול לגברא. לא היה שאול מכיר במעשיו של שמואל, וסבר שישאל שכר:
rashi.eng: *and what shall we bring to the man.* Jonathan paraphrases: If he accepts money, what shall we bring to the man? Saul was not familiar with Samuel’s practice and thought that he would ask for a reward.

rashi.heb:
*ותשורה.* 
תרגם יונתן: ומדעם דכשר, לשון יושר. ומנחם פירש: 'תשורה', לשון תקרובת, ראות פני מלך ואדם חשוב, לשון אשורנו (במדבר כד יז), ונראין דבריו:
rashi.eng: *and there is no present.* (Heb ‘t’shurah’) Jonathan renders: and there is nothing proper. This is an expression of ‘yosher,’ propriety. (The root is ‘yashor.’ The yud is missing, and the ‘tav’ is a prefix.) Menahem, however, explains ‘t’shurah’ as an expression of an offering for the privilege of seeing a king or an important person. An expression related to ‘ashurenu,’ “I behold them” (Num. 24: 17). And his opinion is acceptable to me.

notes.220: (sn): A quarter shekel of silver would weigh about a tenth of an ounce (about 3 grams).

rashi.heb:
*רבע שקל.* 
זוזא חדא דכספא:
rashi.eng: *a fourth of a shekel.* one zuz of silver (from Jonathan).

rashi.heb:
*לפנים בישראל.* 
הסופר כתב זאת, ואין זה מדברי נער שאול:
rashi.eng: *Formerly in Israel.* The author wrote this. This is not part of the statement of Saul’s servant.

rashi.heb:
*כי לנביא היום.* 
למי שקורים אותו נביא היום, היו קורים לפנים 'רואה':
rashi.eng: *for he who is called prophet today.* (lit., to the prophet today.) The one who is called a prophet today, was formerly called a seer.

notes.223: (tc): The MT has “him” (אֹתוֹ, ’oto) here, in addition to the “him” at the end of the verse. The ancient versions attest to only one occurrence of the pronoun, although it is possible that this is due to translation technique rather than to their having a Hebrew text with the pronoun used only once. The present translation assumes textual duplication in the MT and does not attempt to represent the pronoun twice. However, for a defense of the MT here, with the suggested translation “for him just now – you will find him,” see S. R. Driver, Notes on the Hebrew Text and the Topography of the Books of Samuel, 72-73.

rashi.heb:
*כבואכם העיר כן וגו'.* 
מאריכות היו בדברים, כדי להסתכל ביופיו של שאול:
rashi.eng: *When you come to the city, straightway.* They prolonged their conversation in order to gaze upon Saul’s handsomeness.

rashi.heb:
*הבמתה.* 
תרגם יונתן: לבית אסחרותא. משחרבה שילה הותרו הבמות, והיו מקריבין שלמים בבמה, ואוכלים יחד:
rashi.eng: *to the high place.* Jonathan renders: to the banquet hall. When Shiloh was destroyed, the high places were permitted, and they would sacrifice peace- offerings in the high place and eat together.

rashi.heb:
*כי הוא יברך הזבח.* 
תרגם יונתן: 'ארי הוא פריס מזונא', בוצע על המזון, על השלמים מברכין באכילתם: ברוך אתה ה' אלהינו מלך העולם אשר קדשנו במצותיו וצונו לאכול את הזבח:
rashi.eng: *for he will bless the sacrifice.* Jonathan renders: for he will break bread. For the peace-offering they recited the following benediction: Blessed are You, O Lord our God, King of the universe, Who has sanctified us with His commandments, and commanded us to eat the sacrifice.

rashi.heb:
*כהיום.* 
כאשר היום קיים:
rashi.eng: *at this time.* just as the day exists.

notes.224: (tn, Heb): “to meet them.” This may indicate purpose on Samuel’s part. The next sentence indicates that the meeting was by design, not just an accident.

rashi.heb:
*יעצר בעמי.* 
ימשול, (ספרים אחרים אינו) כמו (דברים לב לו): עצור ועזוב. כך דרך המושל, לעצור העם במלחמה, שלא יתפזרו ולא יתפשטו זה מזה, ולעצור בכל אחד מעשות רעה בלשוננו קורין 'מעצור', קירשטני"ר בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *will rule over My people.* (Heb. ‘yazor,’ will restrain,) meaning ‘will rule,’ similar to “restrained (azur) and let free” (Deut. 32:36). So is the function of the ruler, viz., to restrain the people during a war, that they do not scatter, and that they do not spread out from one another, and to restrain everyone from doing evil. In our language, we call ‘maazor’ (restraint) contenir, in French.

rashi.heb:
*ויגש.* 
תרגם יונתן: וערע:
rashi.eng: *approached Samuel.* (The Heb. is ‘vayigash,’ accompanied by ‘eth’ instead of the usual ‘el’, to. Therefore,) Jonathan interprets this as: And Saul met Samuel (similar to ‘vayifgash’).

notes.228: (tn, Heb): “all that is in your heart.”

notes.230: (tn, Heb): “and all the house of your father.”

rashi.heb:
*ולמי כל חמדת ישראל.* 
כאן בא לרמוז לו דבר המלוכה:
rashi.eng: *and to whom does all that is desirable in Israel belong?.* He came here to hint to him the matter of the kingdom.

rashi.heb:
*בראש הקרואים.* 
במקום מסיבת הגדולים, כי בדרך מסיבתן היה ניכר איזה מקום מיסב הגדול:
rashi.eng: *at the head of the invited guests.* in the place where the most important people are seated, for from the manner of the seating, it was apparent in which place the most important person sat.

rashi.heb:
*אשר אמרתי אליך.* 
לפי שידע שמואל שיבא שאול, צוה לתת לו מנה יפה לצרכו:
rashi.eng: *which I said to you.* Since Samuel knew that Saul would come, he ordered to give him a handsome portion for his benefit.

notes.232: (tn, Heb): “he” (also in v. 25); the referent (Samuel) has been specified in both places in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*את השוק והעליה.* 
את השוק והירך שעליה:
rashi.eng: *the thigh and that which was upon it.* I.e., the thigh and the hip which is above it.

rashi.heb:
*הנה הנשאר.* 
מן המנות של הקרואים, והוצב לבד לצרכך:
rashi.eng: *Behold that which has been reserved.* from the portions of the invited guests, and has been set aside for you.

rashi.heb:
*שים לפניך אכול.* 
בפרק אחרון דזבחים (קכ א): קיימא לן חזה ושוק בבמה גדולה, ואין חזה ושוק בבמה קטנה, לפיכך הותר לאכול לשאול:
rashi.eng: *Place (it) before you (and) eat.* In the final chapter of Tractate Zeb. 119b, it is established that (the waving of) the breast and thigh is (practiced) in a large (public) high place, but the waving of the breast and thigh is not (practiced) in a small (private) high place. It was, therefore, permissible for Saul to eat.

rashi.heb:
*כי למועד שמור.* 
כי למועד האכילה היה השוק הזה שמור לצרכך:
rashi.eng: *because for the appointed time it is reserved.* because for the appointed time of the banquet, this thigh was reserved for you.

rashi.heb:
*לאמר העם קראתי.* 
אמירתי היתה לטבח העם, קראתי לסעודה, ויודע אני מספרם, והזהר במנותם, ונתתי לו המנות למספרם, וזו שמורה לצורכך:
rashi.eng: *by saying, “I have invited the people.”.* My statement was to the cook, (as follows): ‘I invited the people to the feast, and I know their number. Be careful with their portions.’ And I gave (assigned) him the portions according to their number, and this was reserved for you.

rashi.heb:
*וידבר עם שאול על הגג.* 
מוכיחו ומלמדו ליראה את הקב"ה:
rashi.eng: *and he spoke with Saul on the roof.* reproving him and teaching him to fear the Holy One, Blessed be He.

notes.233: (tc): This statement is absent in the LXX (with the exception of Origen), an Old Latin ms, and the Syriac Peshitta.
notes.234: (tn): The words “Samuel then said” are supplied in the translation for clarification and for stylistic reasons.

rashi.heb:
*ויעבר לפנינו.* 
וילך ברחוק ממנו, ולא ישמע את דברינו
rashi.eng: *to go ahead of us.* to go far from us so that he will not overhear our conversation.

rashi.heb:
*ויעבר.* 
הנער לפניהם, ולשאול אמר: ואתה עמוד עמדי:
rashi.eng: *and he went ahead.* The servant went ahead of them, and to Saul he said, “And you stand still with me.”

notes.235: (tn, Heb): “his”; the referent (Saul) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.236: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Samuel) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.237: (tn, Heb): “Is it not that the Lord has anointed you?” The question draws attention to the fact and is a rhetorical way of affirming the Lord’s choice of Saul. The translation reflects the rhetorical force of the question.
notes.239: (tc): The MT reads simply “Is it not that the Lord has anointed you over his inheritance for a leader?” The translation follows the LXX. The MT apparently suffers from parablepsis, whereby a scribe’s eye jumped from the first occurrence of the expression “the Lord has anointed you” to the second occurrence of this expression at the end of v. 1. This mistake caused the accidental omission of the intervening material in the LXX, which appears to preserve the original Hebrew text here.

notes.240: (sn): In the Hebrew text the pronoun you is plural, suggesting that Saul’s father was concerned about his son and the servant who accompanied him.

rashi.heb:
*עם קבורת רחל בגבול בנימן.* 
והלא קבורת רחל בגבול יהודה בבית לחם, אלא עכשיו הם בקבורת רחל, וכשתפגע בהם תמצאם בגבול בנימן בצלצח, כך שנויה בתוספתא דסוטה (פרק יא):
rashi.eng: *by Rachel’s tomb, in the border of Benjamin.* Now, isn’t Rachel’s tomb in the border of Judah, in Bethlehem? Rather, (this is the meaning:) Now, they are by Rachel’s tomb, and when you will meet them, you will find them in the border of Benjamin, in Zelzah. Thus taught the Rabbis in the Tosefta of Tractate Sotah.

rashi.heb:
*צלצח.* 
צל לצח של הקב"ה, שהוא צח ואדום, והיא ירושלים:
rashi.eng: *Zelzah.* Zelzah is a combination of the words: ‘zel l’zah,’ the shadow of the Fair One, of the Holy One, Blessed be He, Who is fair and ruddy (So described in Song of Songs 5:10). And this is Jerusalem.

rashi.heb:
*ודאג לכם.* 
יירא עליכם, כל לשון 'דאגה', לשון 'יראה', דושטי"ר בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *is worried.* fears concerning you, and likewise, every expression of worry (d’agah) is an expression of fear. Douter in French.

notes.241: (map): For location see Map4-G4; Map5-C1; Map6-E3; Map7-D1; Map8-G3.

rashi.heb:
*אילון תבור.* 
מישר תבור:
rashi.eng: *אילון תבור.* the plain of Tabor.

notes.242: (tn): Or “sentries.” Some translate “outpost” (NIV) or “garrison” (NAB, NRSV, NLT) here (see 1 Sam 13:3). The noun is plural in the Hebrew text, but the LXX and other ancient witnesses read a singular noun here.

rashi.heb:
*גבעת האלהים.* 
גבעת קרית יערים, אשר עכשיו ארון האלהים שם:
rashi.eng: *the hill of God.* the hill of Kiriath-jearim, where the Ark of God was now (stationed).

rashi.heb:
*נציבי פלשתים.* 
סרדיוטות שמינו על ישראל, שהיו רודין בה, ומושיבים נציבים בערי ישראל:
rashi.eng: *Philistine officers.* officers whom they had appointed over Israel for they were ruling over them and stationing officers in the cities of Israel.

rashi.heb:
*חבל נביאים.* 
תרגם יונתן: סיעת ספריא: חבל. סיעה, וכן (שמואל-ב כב ו): חבלי שאול סבוני, משרית רשיעיא אקפוני:
rashi.eng: *a band of prophets.* (Heb. ‘hevel n’viim’) Jonathan renders: a band of scribes. ‘Hevel’ is a band. Likewise, “The bands of sheol surrounded me” (II Sam. 22:6) is rendered: The camps of the wicked surrounded me.

rashi.heb:
*מהבמה.* 
תרגם יונתן: מבית אסחרותא:
rashi.eng: *from the high place.* Jonathan renders from the banquet hall.

notes.243: (sn): In light of Saul’s commission to be Israel’s deliverer (see v. 1), it is likely that some type of military action against the Philistines (see v.5) is implied.

rashi.heb:
*כי תבאנה האותות האלה לך.* 
ותדע כי דברי אמת, וכשם שבאו לך אותות הללו, כך יתקיים דבר המלוכה:
rashi.eng: *And it will be that when these signs will come to you.* And you will know that my words are true, for just as these signs will have come to you, so will the matter of the kingdom be fulfilled.

rashi.heb:
*עשה לך אשר תמצא ידך.* 
אתקין לך מאני מלכותא, והכן לך טכסיסי המלוכה כמו שתוכל:
rashi.eng: *do for yourself what your hand will find.* Prepare for yourself regal garments (Jonathan), and prepare for yourself the court ceremonial.

rashi.heb:
*וירדת לפני הגלגל.* 
ולאחר שתמלוך, תרד הגלגל לפני, קודם שארד אני:
rashi.eng: *And you shall come down before me to Gilgal.* And after you reign, you shall come down to Gilgal before me, i.e., before I come down.

rashi.heb:
*והנה אנכי ירד אליך.* 
לסוף שבעת ימים שתרד אתה:
rashi.eng: *and behold, I shall go down to you.* at the termination of seven days after you will have gone down.

rashi.heb:
*תוחל.* 
תמתין:
rashi.eng: *shall you wait.* shall you wait.

notes.244: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Saul) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.246: (tn, Heb): “God turned for him another heart”; NAB, NRSV “gave him another heart”; NIV, NCV “changed Saul’s heart”; TEV “gave Saul a new nature”; CEV “made Saul feel like a different person.”

rashi.heb:
*לב אחר.* 
רוח גבורת מלכות:
rashi.eng: *another heart.* a spirit of regal power.

notes.247: (tc, Heb): Two medieval Hebrew mss, the LXX, and the Syriac Peshitta have the singular “he” (in which case the referent would be Saul alone). “they”; the referents (Saul and his servant) have been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.248: (tn, Heb): “him”; the referent (Saul) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*ומי אביהם.* 
מה תימה לך בדבר מי אביהם של נביאים, וכי נבואה ירושה היא:
rashi.eng: *And who is their father?.* Why do you wonder about the matter “Who is the father of the prophets? Is prophecy hereditary?”

notes.249: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Saul) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

notes.250: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Saul) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.251: (tn, Heb): “And we saw that they were not.”

notes.252: (tc): In the LXX and Vulgate the pronoun “you” is singular, referring specifically to Saul. In the MT it is plural, including Saul’s servant as well.

notes.253: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Saul) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*ואת דבר המלוכה לא הגיד.* 
דרך צניעות היתה בו:
rashi.eng: *and the matter of the kingdom he did not tell him..* He possessed the trait of discretion.

notes.255: (tc): The translation follows many medieval Hebrew mss, the LXX, the Syriac Peshitta, and Vulgate in reading לֹא (lo’, “not”) rather than the MT לוֹ (lo; “to him”). Some witnesses combine the variants, resulting in a conflated text. For example, a few medieval Hebrew mss have לֹא לוֹ (lo lo’; “to him, ‘No.’”). A few others have לֹא לִי (li lo’; “to me, ‘No.’”).

rashi.heb:
*וילכד שאול.* 
אף על פי שלא היה שם, נפל הגורל עליו, שהיו כתובין שמם באיגרות ונתונין בקופסא, והנביא מכניס ידו ונוטל איגרת אחת:
rashi.eng: *and Saul… was taken.* Even though he was not there, the lot fell upon him, for their names were written on pieces of parchment and placed in a box. Now the Prophet would insert his hand and take one piece of parchment.

notes.256: (tn): Or “baggage” (so many English versions); KJV “stuff”; TEV “supplies.”

rashi.heb:
*נחבא אל הכלים.* 
בבית שנתנו שם הבאין כליהן, שהיה בורח מן הגדולה ומדרש אגדה רבי תנחומא: ואל הכלים, באורים ותומים, אמר: שמא איני ראוי לגדולה עד שישאלו באורים ותומים, ושאלו ועלה בידו:
rashi.eng: *is hidden among the baggage.* (Heb. ‘el hakelim,’ lit., to the vessels,) to the house where the comers had placed their baggage. (He did this) because he was fleeing the high position. And the Midrash Agadah of Rabbi Tanhuma (Levit. 1) explains: ‘to the vessels’ as referring to the Urim and Tummim. He said, ‘Perhaps I am not worthy of this high position. (I shall not assume it) until they ask of the Urim and Tummim.’ Thereupon they asked, and he achieved it.

notes.257: (tn, Heb): “the regulation of the kingship.” This probably refers to the regulations pertaining to kingship given to Moses (see Deut 17:14-20).

rashi.heb:
*אשר נגע אלהים.* 
גברין דחלי חטאה דאתיהב דחלא מן קדם ה' בלבהון:
rashi.eng: *whose heart God had touched.* (Jonathan renders:) sin fearing men, in whose heart God had given fear.

notes.259: (tc): In place of the MT (“and it was like one being silent”) the LXX has “after about a month,” taking the expression with the first part of the following chapter rather than with 10:27. Some Hebrew support for this reading appears in the corrected hand of a Qumran ms of Samuel, which has here “about a month.” However, it seems best to stay with the MT here even though it is difficult.

notes.260: (tc): 4QSama and Josephus (Ant. 6.68-71) attest to a longer form of text at this point. The addition explains Nahash’s practice of enemy mutilation, and by so doing provides a smoother transition to the following paragraph than is found in the MT. The NRSV adopts this reading, with the following English translation: “Now Nahash, king of the Ammonites, had been grievously oppressing the Gadites and the Reubenites. He would gouge out the right eye of each of them and would not grant Israel a deliverer. No one was left of the Israelites across the Jordan whose right eye Nahash, king of the Ammonites, had not gouged out. But there were seven thousand men who had escaped from the Ammonites and had entered Jabesh-gilead.” This reading should not be lightly dismissed; it may in fact provide a text superior to that of the MT and the ancient versions. But the external evidence for it is so limited as to induce caution; the present translation instead follows the MT. However, for a reasonable case for including this reading in the text see the discussions in P. K. McCarter, I Samuel (AB), 199, and R. W. Klein, 1 Samuel (WBC), 103.
notes.262: (tn, Heb): “went up and camped”; NIV, NRSV “went up and besieged.”

rashi.heb:
*כל עין ימין.* 
כמשמעו ומדרש אגדה (ילקוט שמעוני רמז קיא): הביאו לי ספר תורתכם שנתנה מימין, ואשרפה, על שכתוב בו (דברים כג ד): לא יבא עמוני ומואבי וגו':
rashi.eng: *the right eye.* (We explain this) literally, but the Midrash Agadah (MS. 14:7) (explains it figuratively): He said, “Bring me your Torah which was given by the right hand (of the Almighty),” (Deut. 33:2), and I shall burn it, because He wrote therein: “An Ammonite and a Moabite shall not enter the congregation of the Lord” (Deut. 23:3).

rashi.heb:
*חרפה.* 
גדוף:
rashi.eng: *a reproach.* an insult.

notes.265: (tn): Or perhaps, “his oxen.” On this use of the definite article see Jo�on 2:506-7 �137.f.

rashi.heb:
*אחרי הבקר.* 
אחר זמן מועד ביאת הבקר מן השדה:
rashi.eng: *after the cattle.* after the appointed time that the cattle come in from the field.

rashi.heb:
*לבקרו.* 
לבהמותיו:
rashi.eng: *to his oxen.* to his animals.

notes.269: (tc): The LXX and two Old Latin mss read 600,000 here, rather than the MT’s 300,000.
notes.270: (tc): The LXX, two Old Latin mss, and a Qumran ms read 70,000 here, rather than the MT’s 30,000.

rashi.heb:
*ויפקדם בבזק.* 
רבותינו אמרו (יומא כב ב): בשברי חרסים (ס"א, אינו). לשון אחר: בבזק, באבנים, שנטל מכל אחד אבן ומנאם, כמו (לקמן טו ד): ויפקדם בטלאים, שנטל מכל אחד טלה ומנאם בהם, כמו שהיו מונים אותם בחצאי שקלים, ותרגם (משלי כו ח): כצרור אבן במרגמה, היך בזקא דכיפא בקלעא. ובילמדנו: ויפקדם בטלאים, כד אינון מסכנין, באלין בזקייא, כד אינון עתירים, באלין אימריא. לשון אחר: 'בבזק', שם מקום הנזכר בספר שופטים (א ה) וימצאו את אדוני בזק בבזק:
rashi.eng: *And he counted them in Bezek.* Our Rabbis said: (He counted them) with fragments of earthenware. (I. e., ‘bezek’ is a common noun, not the name of a place.) (Yoma 22b) (The following does not appear in certain editions of Rashi.) Another explanation is that ‘b’vezek’ means ‘with pebbles,’ i.e., he took a pebble from each one, and counted them, similar to “And he counted them with lambs” (infra 15:4), which means that he took a lamb from each one, and counted them therewith, just as they would count them with half shekels. In (Prov. 26: 8) “like a pebble for throwing in a slingshot,” the Targum uses the word ‘bizka.’ And in Midrash Yelam’denu (T. Ki Thissa 9, Buber 8) “And he counted them with lambs.” When they were poor, they were counted with pebbles; when they became rich, they were counted with lambs. Another explanation is that ‘bezek’ is the name of a place, mentioned (in Judges 1:5): “And they found Adoni-bezek in Bezek.”

notes.271: (tn): The second masculine plural forms in this quotation indicate that Nahash and his army are addressed.
notes.272: (tn, Heb): “according to all that is good in your eyes.”

notes.273: (tn, Heb): “Ammon.” By metonymy the name “Ammon” is used collectively for the soldiers in the Ammonite army.

rashi.heb:
*מי האומר.* 
בלשון בזיון, שאול ימלוך עלינו, תנו אותם ונמיתם:
rashi.eng: *Whosoever says.* derisively, “Saul will reign over us?” give them over, and let us put them to death.

rashi.heb:
*ימלוך עלינו.* 
בתמיה:
rashi.eng: *will reign.* as a question.

rashi.heb:
*ויאמר שמואל וגו' ונחדש שם המלוכה.* 
לפי שבראשונה היו עוררים על הדבר, ועתה נתרצו כולם:
rashi.eng: *And Samuel said, etc.,… and let us renew there the kingdom.* Since previously, there was opposition in the matter, and now they were all agreeable.

notes.275: (tn, Heb): “Look, I have listened to your voice.”
notes.276: (tn, Heb): “to all which you said to me.”
notes.277: (tn, Heb): “and I have installed a king over you.”

rashi.heb:
*ואני זקנתי ושבתי.* 
אמרו רבותינו: זקנה קפצה עליו, כדאיתא במסכת תענית (ה ב):
rashi.eng: *and I have become old and hoary.* Our Rabbis said that he aged prematurely, as it is stated in Tractate Taanith (5b).

notes.279: (tn): The words “tell me” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.

rashi.heb:
*את שור מי לקחתי.* 
לעבודתי:
rashi.eng: *whose ox did I take.* for my work.

rashi.heb:
*וחמור מי לקחתי.* 
כשהייתי הולך מעיר לעיר לשפוט אותם על עסקי צרכיהם, הייתי הולך על החמור שלי, והיה לי ליטול משלהם:
rashi.eng: *or whose ass did I take.* When I used to go from city to city to judge them concerning their needs, I used to go on my own ass, although I should have taken (one) of theirs.

rashi.heb:
*את מי רצותי.* 
כל לשון מרוצה הסמוך לעושק, לשון עשוק ורצוץ הוא, חומס דלים ורוצץ:
rashi.eng: *or whom did I oppress.* Every expression of ‘meruzah’ which follows ‘oshek’ (robbery), is an expression of “robbed and oppressed” (Deut. 28:33), one who robs the poor and oppresses them.

rashi.heb:
*ואעלים עיני בו.* 
כדי להעלים עיני מן המשפט בשביל הממון:
rashi.eng: *that I hide my eyes therewith.* in order to hide my eyes from the judgment because of the money.

rashi.heb:
*ואשיב לכם.* 
כל מה שתאמרו:
rashi.eng: *and I shall restore to you.* all that you will say.

notes.281: (tn, Heb): “that you have not found anything in my hand.”

rashi.heb:
*ויאמר עד.* 
בת קול יוצאת ואומרת: 'עד', וזה אחד משלשה מקומות שהופיעה רוח הקודש בבית דין של מטה, כדאיתא במסכת מכות (כג ב):
rashi.eng: *and they said, “(He is) witness.”.* (lit., ‘and he said.’ The Rabbis, taking the word literally, explain that) a bath kol (a heavenly voice) came forth and said, ‘I am witness.’ This was one of three places in which the holy spirit entered the earthly court, as it is stated in Tractate Makkoth (23b).

rashi.heb:
*אשר עשה את משה ואת אהרן.* 
להיות נכונים לשליחותו, להוציא אבותיכם ממצרים:
rashi.eng: *Who made Moses and Aaron.* to be prepared for His mission to take your forefathers out of Egypt.

notes.283: (tn, Heb): “and I will enter into judgment with you” (NRSV similar); NAB “and I shall arraign you.”
notes.284: (tn, Heb): “all the just actions which he has done with you and with your fathers.”

rashi.heb:
*ואשפטה אתכם.* 
אתוכח עמכם:
rashi.eng: *and I shall reason.* or debate.

notes.285: (tn, Heb): “sold” (so KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV); NAB “he allowed them to fall into the clutches of Sisera”; NLT “he let them be conquered by Sisera.”
notes.286: (map): For location see Map1-D2; Map2-D3; Map3-A2; Map4-C1.
notes.287: (tn, Heb): “captain of the host of Hazor.”

notes.289: (tn, Heb): “the Ashtarot” (plural). The words “images of” are supplied in both vv. 3 and 4 for clarity. The Semitic goddess Astarte was associated with love and war in the ancient Near East. See the note on the same term in 7:3.
notes.290: (tn): After the imperative, the prefixed verbal form with the prefixed conjunction indicates purpose/result.

notes.291: (sn): Jerub-Baal (יְרֻבַּעַל) is also known as Gideon (see Judg 6:32). The Book of Judges uses both names for him.
notes.292: (tc): The MT has “Bedan” (בְּדָן) here (cf. KJV, NASB, CEV). But a deliverer by this name is not elsewhere mentioned in the OT. The translation follows the LXX and the Syriac Peshitta in reading “Barak.”
notes.293: (tc): In the ancient versions there is some confusion with regard to these names, both with regard to the particular names selected for mention and with regard to the order in which they are listed. For example, the LXX has “Jerub-Baal, Barak, Jephthah, and Samuel.” But the Targum has “Gideon, Samson, Jephthah, and Samuel,” while the Syriac Peshitta has “Deborah, Barak, Gideon, Jephthah, and Samson.”

rashi.heb:
*ירובעל.* 
זה גדעון:
rashi.eng: *Jerubaal.* This is Gideon (Jud. 6:32).

rashi.heb:
*בדן.* 
זה שמשון, שמשבט דן בא:
rashi.eng: *Bedan.* This is Samson who came from the tribe of Dan.

rashi.heb:
*ואת יפתח.* 
הרי שלשה קלי עולם, עם שלשה חמורי עולם, משה ואהרן ושמואל, לומר לך, הקל בדורו, כחמור בדורו, כל בית דין המתמנה על הדור, צריך לילך אחריו כאלו הוא אביר שבאבירים:
rashi.eng: *and Jephthah.* Here are three insignificant leaders with three eminent leaders: Moses, Aaron, and Samuel, to tell you that the insignificant leader in his generation is equal to the eminent leader in his generation. Every court which is appointed over the generation must be followed as though its members were the noblest of nobility.

notes.294: (tn, Heb): “and you listen to his voice.”
notes.295: (tn, Heb): “the mouth of the Lord.” So also in v. 15.
notes.296: (tn): The words “all will be well” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.

rashi.heb:
*והיתם גם אתם.* 
ותתקיימו לאורך ימים גם אתם גם המלך:
rashi.eng: *both you and the king who reigns over you will be.* Both you and the king who reigns over you will live to a ripe old age.

notes.298: (tc): The LXX reads “your king” rather than the MT’s “your fathers.” The latter makes little sense here. Some follow MT, but translate “as it was against your fathers.” See P. K. McCarter, 1 Samuel (AB), 212.

rashi.heb:
*והיתה יד ה' בכם ובאבותיכם.* 
כלומר והיתה בכם אחר שהיתה באבותיכם ורבותינו אמרו (יבמות סג ב): בכם ובאבותיכם, חטוטי שכבי, והיא מכת בזיון על המתים:
rashi.eng: *the Lord’s hand will be against you and against your fathers.* Meaning, after it was against your fathers. Our Rabbis, however, said: (Jeb. 63b) “against you and against your fathers” refers to the digging up of the dead, which is a visitation of disgrace upon the dead.

rashi.heb:
*התיצבו וראו וגו'.* 
וכשם שעל ידי תפלתי אני יכול לשנות את העתים, כך אם פגעה בכם מלחמה, היה כח בתפלתי לעמוד על האויב, ולא הייתם צריכים לשאול מלך בחיי, ואף על פי שאני זקן:
rashi.eng: *stand and see, etc..* and just as through my prayer, I am able to change the seasons, similarly, if a war befell you, there would be power in my prayer to protect you against the adversary, and you had no need to ask for a king during my lifetime despite the fact that I am old.

rashi.heb:
*הלא קציר חטים היום.* 
והגשמים סימן קללה, וקשה בעיני הקב"ה להביא פורענות חנם, אף על פי כן יש בי כח, ואקרא אל ה' ויתן קולות ומטר:
rashi.eng: *Is it not wheat harvest today?.* Rain is an evil omen (Taanith 12b), and the Holy One Blessed be He is reluctant to visit retribution for nothing. Nevertheless, I have power; I shall call to the Lord, and He will send thunder and rain.

rashi.heb:
*ודעו וראו.* 
כי לא הייתם צריכים לשאול מלך לזלזל בי:
rashi.eng: *and you shall know and see.* that it was unnecessary to ask for a king and to treat me with disrespect.

notes.299: (tn, Heb): “for we have added to all our sins an evil [thing] by asking for ourselves a king.”

notes.300: (tn, Heb): “you have done all this evil.”

notes.301: (tn): Or “useless” (so NIV, NRSV, NLT); NAB “nothing”; NASB “futile”; TEV “are not real.”

notes.302: (tn, Heb): “on account of his great name.”

rashi.heb:
*בעבור שמו הגדול.* 
אשר יצא שמו עליכם שהוא מושיעכם, ולמען לא יתמעט שם גדלו:
rashi.eng: *for His great Name’s sake.* for His Name has spread concerning you, that He is your Savior and lest the Name of His greatness be diminished.

rashi.heb:
*הואיל ה'.* 
נשבע, כמו (לקמן יד כה): ויואל שאול את העם:
rashi.eng: *the Lord swore.* (Heb. ‘ho il,’) like (infra 14:24) “And Saul made the people swear (Heb. ‘vayoel’).”

rashi.heb:
*גם אנכי חלילה לי.* 
מאחר שתעשו אתם את שלכם לשוב אל ה', גם אנכי חלילה לי מחדול מהתפלל בעדכם:
rashi.eng: *also far be it from me.* Since you will do your part by returning to the Lord, I also, far be it from me to stop praying for you.

notes.303: (tc): The MT does not have “thirty.” A number appears to have dropped out of the Hebrew text here, since as it stands the MT (literally, “a son of a year”) must mean that Saul was only one year old when he began to reign! The KJV, attempting to resolve this, reads “Saul reigned one year,” but that is not the normal meaning of the Hebrew text represented by the MT. Although most LXX mss lack the entire verse, some Greek mss have “thirty years” here (while others have “one year” like the MT). The Syriac Peshitta has Saul’s age as twenty-one. But this seems impossible to harmonize with the implied age of Saul’s son Jonathan in the following verse. Taking into account the fact that in v. 2 Jonathan was old enough to be a military leader, some scholars prefer to supply in v. 1 the number forty (cf. ASV, NASB). The present translation (“thirty”) is a possible but admittedly uncertain proposal based on a few Greek mss and followed by a number of English versions (e.g., NIV, NCV, NLT). Other English versions simply supply ellipsis marks for the missing number (e.g., NAB, NRSV).
notes.304: (tc): The MT has “two years” here. If this number is to be accepted as correct, the meaning apparently would be that after a lapse of two years at the beginning of Saul’s reign, he then went about the task of consolidating an army as described in what follows (cf. KJV, ASV, CEV). But if the statement in v. 1 is intended to be a comprehensive report on the length of Saul’s reign, the number is too small. According to Acts 13:21 Saul reigned for forty years. Some English versions (e.g., NIV, NCV, NLT), taking this forty to be a round number, add it to the “two years” of the MT and translate the number in 2 Sam 13:1 as “forty-two years.” While this is an acceptable option, the present translation instead replaces the MT’s “two” with the figure “forty.” Admittedly the textual evidence for this decision is weak, but the same can be said of any attempt to restore sense to this difficult text (note the ellipsis marks at this point in NAB, NRSV). The Syriac Peshitta lacks this part of v. 1.

rashi.heb:
*בן שנה שאול במלכו.* 
אמרו רבותינו ז"ל (יומא כב ב): כבן שנה, שלא טעם טעם חטא. ויש לפתור: בן שנה שאול במלכו, בשנה ראשונה שהומלך בה, והוא מלך שתי שנים על ישראל, ובשנה ראשונה, מיד: ויבחר לו שאול שלשת אלפים:
rashi.eng: *Saul was a year in his reign.* (lit., a year old.) Our Rabbis of sainted memory said: Like a one year old, who did not experience the taste of sin (Yoma 22b). It may also be interpreted thus: Saul was a year in his reign, i.e., in the first year in which he was made king (and he reigned two years over Israel), and in the first year, immediately, Saul chose for himself three thousand.

notes.305: (map): For location see Map4-G4; Map5-C1; Map6-E3; Map7-D1; Map8-G3.
notes.306: (tn, Heb): “at Gibeah of Benjamin.” The words “in the territory” are supplied in the translation for clarity.

notes.308: (tn): Or perhaps “struck down the Philistine official.” See the note at 1 Sam 10:5. Cf. TEV “killed the Philistine commander.”

rashi.heb:
*את נציב פלשתים.* 
סרדיוט שהיה להם על ישראל, והושיבוהו בגבעת בנימן:
rashi.eng: *the officer of the Philistines.* They had an officer over Israel whom they had stationed in Gibeah of Benjamin.

rashi.heb:
*ישמעו העברים.* 
שמרדנו בפלשתים, וישמרו מהם:
rashi.eng: *Let the Hebrews hear.* that we have rebelled against the Philistines, and let them beware of them.

notes.310: (tn): The words “this message” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.
notes.311: (tn, Heb): “stinks.” The figurative language indicates that Israel had become repulsive to the Philistines.

rashi.heb:
*וגם נבאש ישראל.* 
נבאש ריחם בפלשתים, לשון 'שנאה':
rashi.eng: *and also Israel has become hateful.* Lit., they have come in bad odor with the Philistines. An expression of hatred.

rashi.heb:
*אחרי שאול הגלגל.* 
הוא שאמר לו שמואל (לעיל י ח) וירדת לפני הגלגל:
rashi.eng: *after Saul to Gilgal.* This is what Samuel had said to him (supra 10: 8), “And you shall come down before me to Gilgal.”

notes.313: (tn): Many English versions (e.g., KJV, NASB, NRSV, TEV) read “30,000” here.

rashi.heb:
*קדמת בית און.* 
במזרח בית און:
rashi.eng: *to the east of Beth-aven.* (Heb. ‘kidmath’) same as ‘mizrach’ Beth- aven.

notes.314: (tn): Or perhaps “vaults.” This rare term also occurs in Judg 9:46, 49. Cf. KJV “high places”; ASV “coverts”; NAB “caverns”; NASB “cellars”; NIV, NCV, TEV “pits”; NRSV, NLT “tombs.”

rashi.heb:
*ובחוחים.* 
מקום קבוצת חוחים, שפנ"י בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *and in the thickets.* a place where thorns are concentrated. Epine in French (thorn).

rashi.heb:
*ובצרחים.* 
פליישי"ץ בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *and in the towers.* (as a forest in which the trees and branches are bent over all around the forest,) Plisse in French (folded).

rashi.heb:
*ובבורות.* 
גומות:
rashi.eng: *and in the pits.* Holes [in the ground].

notes.315: (tn): The word “River” is not in the Hebrew text, but has been supplied in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*עברו את הירדן ארץ גד.* 
לברוח מפני פלשתים, שהפלשתים היו בארץ כנען בעבר הירדן ימה:
rashi.eng: *And some Hebrews crossed the Jordan to the land of Gad.* to flee from before the Philistines since the Philistines were in the land of Canaan on the west side of the Jordan.

rashi.heb:
*חרדו אחריו.* 
מהרו ללכת אחריו:
rashi.eng: *hurried after him.* (lit. trembled after him;) i.e., they hurried to go after him.

notes.316: (tn): This apparently refers to the instructions given by Samuel in 1 Sam 10:8. If so, several years had passed. On the relationship between chs. 10 and 13, see V. P. Long, The Art of Biblical History (FCI), 201-23.
notes.317: (tn, Heb): “dispersed from upon him”; NAB, NRSV “began to slip away.”

rashi.heb:
*ויוחל.* 
המתין:
rashi.eng: *ויוחל.* And he waited.

rashi.heb:
*למועד אשר שמואל.* 
הרי זה מקרא חסר תיבה אחת, למועד אשר שם שמואל' או למועד אשר לשמואל, ודוגמא לו (שמואל-ב ד ב): ושני אנשים שרי גדודים היו בן שאול, היה לו לכתוב לבן שאול, אף כאן אשר לשמואל, שאמר לו (לעיל י ח) שבעת ימים תוחל עד בואי אליך:
rashi.eng: *to the appointed time which Samuel.* this is a short verse, with one word missing. (We must explain:) to the appointed time which Samuel had set, or to the appointed time of Samuel. And an example of this, we find (II Samuel 4:2) “And two men, officers of troops were the son of Saul.” He should have written: were to the son of Saul (or the son of Saul had). Here too, ‘which was to Samuel’ (or ‘of Samuel’), who said to him, “Seven days shall you wait until I come to you” (supra 10:8).

rashi.heb:
*הגישו אלי העולה.* 
זר מותר להקריב בבמה:
rashi.eng: *Bring near to me the burnt offering.* A stranger (non-priest) is permitted to sacrifice on a high place.

rashi.heb:
*מה עשית.* 
הלא אמרתי לך הנני יורד אליך להעלות העולה, אני אעלה אותה, ולא אתה:
rashi.eng: *“What have you done?”.* Did I not say to you, ‘Behold I shall come down to you to offer up the burnt offering?’ I should offer it up, and not you.

rashi.heb:
*למועד הימים.* 
בתחלת היום:
rashi.eng: *at the appointed time of the days.* at the beginning of the day.

notes.321: (tn): Or “I forced myself” (so KJV, NASB, NRSV, CEV); NAB “So in my anxiety I offered”; NIV “I felt compelled.”

rashi.heb:
*ואתאפק.* 
נתחזקתי על רצוני, שהיה לבי אומר להמתין לך, על כרחי העמדתי את לבי ואעלה העולה:
rashi.eng: *and I forced myself.* I overcame my will, for my heart told me to wait for you, and against my will I suppressed my heart, and offered up the burnt offering.

rashi.heb:
*כי עתה.* 
לפני עשותך זאת:
rashi.eng: *for now.* Before you did this.

rashi.heb:
*הכין ה' את ממלכתך עד עולם.* 
שכשפוסקין לו גדולה לאדם, פוסקין לו ולדורותיו (מגילה יג ב):
rashi.eng: *the Lord would have established your kingdom over Israel forever.* for when a high position is assigned to a person, it is assigned to him and to his posterity.

notes.324: (tn): This verb form, as well as the one that follows (“appointed”), indicates completed action from the standpoint of the speaker. This does not necessarily mean that the Lord had already conducted his search and made his choice, however. The forms may be used for rhetorical effect to emphasize the certainty of the action. The divine search for a new king is as good as done, emphasizing that the days of Saul’s dynasty are numbered.
notes.325: (tn, Heb): “according to his heart.” The idiomatic expression means to be like-minded with another, as its use in 1 Sam 14:7 indicates.

rashi.heb:
*ועתה ממלכתך לא תקום.* 
שכן אמר משה בתורה (דברים יז כ): לבלתי סור מן המצוה ימין ושמאל למען יאריך ימים וגו', הא אם סר, לא יאריך ימים, ואם תאמר לא על מצות נביא נאמר, אלא על מצות התורה, הרי כבר נאמר (שם שם): לשמור את כל דברי התורה הזאת, ואחר כך: לבלתי רום לבבו ולבלתי סור מן המצוה, אפילו ממצות נביא:
rashi.eng: *But now, your kingdom shall not continue.* for so said Moses in the Torah, “and that he turn not aside from the commandment right or left, in order that he prolong his days, etc.” (Deut. 17:20). Hence, if he turns aside, he will not prolong his days. And if you will argue that this was not said in reference to a commandment of a Prophet, but only in reference to a commandment of the Torah, (I shall answer you that) it was already stated: “and to observe all the words of the Law,” and afterwards, “that his heart be not lifted up above his brothers, and that he turn not aside from the commandment,” (meaning) even from a commandment of a Prophet.

notes.327: (tc): The LXX and two Old Latin mss include the following words here: “on his way. And the rest of the people went up after Saul to meet the warring army. When they arrived from Gilgal….”
notes.328: (tn, Heb): “at Gibeah of Benjamin.” The words “in the territory” are supplied in the translation for clarity (likewise in the following verse).

rashi.heb:
*הנמצאים עמו.* 
כי העם נפוצו מעליו, ואלו נשתיירו:
rashi.eng: *who were present with him.* (lit., who were found with him) for the people had scattered from him, and these remained.

notes.329: (tn): The juxtaposition of disjunctive clauses in v.16 indicates synchronic action.

rashi.heb:
*גי הצבועים.* 
שמצויין בו הצבועים, הוא ששנינו, רבי מאיר אומר: אף הצבוע. ותרגם יונתן: אפעיא. וכן פירשו רבותינו ז"ל (בבא קמא טז א): צבוע זה אפעה, מין שרץ רע ומזיק:
rashi.eng: *the valley of the ‘zeboim’.* where the ‘zeboim’ were found. This is the creature referred to by Rabbi Meir when he said: also the zabua (The owner is considered forewarned to pay the full damage the first time it damages B.K. 16a). Jonathan renders: ‘af’aya,’ and so did our Rabbis of sainted memory, explain: ‘zabua’ is ‘eph’eh,’ a species of fierce and destructive reptiles.

rashi.heb:
*וחרש לא ימצא.* 
לא היה מצוי בתחלת מלכות שאול, כי הפלשתים המושלים בישראל, העבירו כל חרשי ברזל מישראל, פן יעשו כלי זיין להלחם:
rashi.eng: *Now, not a smith was to be found.* Not one was found at the beginning of Saul’s reign, because the Philistines who ruled over Israel, dismissed all the ironsmiths from Israel, lest they make weapons to wage war.

notes.330: (tc): The translation follows the LXX (“their sickle”) here, rather than the MT “plowshares,” which is due to dittography from the word earlier in the verse.

rashi.heb:
*וירדו כל ישראל הפלשתים.* 
וכשהיו ישראל צריכין לחרשי ברזל ללטוש איתים וקרדומות ומחרישות, היו זקוקים לירד אל ארץ פלשתים:
rashi.eng: *And all Israel went down (to the land of) the Philistines.* And when the Israelites needed ironsmiths to sharpen colters and axes and mattocks, they were forced to go down to the land of the Philistines.

rashi.heb:
*מחרשתו.* 
שו"ק בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *his plowshare.* (Heb. ‘maharashto’) ‘soc’ in French (a plowshare).

rashi.heb:
*אתו.* 
קולטר"א בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *his colter.* (Heb. ‘eitho’) ‘coutre’ in French (a colter).

rashi.heb:
*קרדומו.* 
בשגו"ר בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *his axe.* (Heb. ‘kardumo’) ‘baisague’ in French (a twibil or axe).

rashi.heb:
*מחרשתו.* 
פישוייר"א בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *his mattock.* (Heb. ‘mahareishatho’) ‘pioche’ in French (a mattock or pickaxe).

notes.331: (tn, Heb): “the price was.” The meaning of the Hebrew word פְּצִירָה (p�tsirah) is uncertain. This is the only place it occurs in the OT. Some propose the meaning “sharpening,” but “price” is a more likely meaning if the following term refers to a weight (see the following note on the word “shekel”). See P. K. McCarter, I Samuel (AB), 238.
notes.332: (tn): This word, which appears only here in the OT, probably refers to a stone weight. Stones marked פִּים (pim) have been found in excavations of Palestinian sites. The average weight of such stones is 0.268 ounces, which is equivalent to about two-thirds of a shekel. This probably refers to the price charged by the Philistines for the services listed. See P. K. McCarter, I Samuel (AB), 238; DNWSI 2:910; and G. I. Davies, Ancient Hebrew Inscriptions, 259.
notes.333: (tc, Heb): “and for a third, a pick.” The Hebrew text suffers from haplography at this point. The translation follows the textual reconstruction offered by P. K. McCarter, I Samuel (AB), 235.

rashi.heb:
*והיתה הפצירה פים למחרשות.* 
והיתה להם לאותם שהיה להם טורח לרדת אל הפלשתים ללטוש, היתה הפצירה פים לימ"א בלע"ז, שיש לה הפצר פיות, כלומר פיות וחידודים הרבה, היתה להם לחדד המחרשת והאתים:
rashi.eng: *And there was the file for the mattocks.* And those who found it overly troublesome to go down to the Philistines to sharpen had an implement called ‘pezirah pim,’ ‘lime’ in French (a file), which has many mouths, i.e., many sharp surfaces. They had this to sharpen the mattocks and the colters.

rashi.heb:
*ולשלש קלשון.* 
מזלג עשוי כמין עתר, שקורין פורקד"א, ולו שלש שינים:
rashi.eng: *and the three pronged pitchforks.* a fork made like a sort of pitchfork, which is called ‘fourche’ (a pitchfork), having three prongs.

rashi.heb:
*ולהציב הדרבן.* 
לחדדו בראשו לנועצו ולהציבו בתוך המרדע:
rashi.eng: *and to set the goad.* to sharpen it at the tip, to insert it, and set it into the handle.

rashi.heb:
*ותמצא לשאול.* 
על ידי נס:
rashi.eng: *but Saul… had them..* (lit., and there was found to Saul) through a miracle.

rashi.heb:
*מצב פלשתים.* 
דרך אנשי צבא לעשות מהם מצב ומשחית, הם הפושטים ורצים אחר השלל אל העיר, שקורין צנבי"ל בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *the garrison of the Philistines.* It is the custom of soldiers to form a garrison and a raiding party. The raiding party is composed of those who spread out into a city in quest of plunder. This is called ‘gens pille’ (plunderers).

rashi.heb:
*מצב.* 
הם נציבים לשמור שלא יצאו מן העיר משחיתים בהם:
rashi.eng: *garrison.* They are the officers who stand guard that no raiders come out of the city against them.

rashi.heb:
*אל מעבר מכמש.* 
הפלשתים היו חונים במכמש, ומכמש בהר, וישראל בעיר ששמה גבע וגבע היתה בראש ההר, ושני הרים היו זה כנגד זה, והגיא ביניהם, כמו שאמור בענין. ומצב פלשתים נגש אל עבר מכמש שלצד גבע, אל הגיא שביניהם:
rashi.eng: *the other side of Michmash.* The Philistines were encamped in Michmash and Michmash was on a mountain. And the Israelites were in a city named Geba and Geba was also at the top of a mountain, and those two mountains were opposite one another, and the valley was between them, as is stated in this episode, “and the garrison of the Philistines approached the other side of Michmash,” which is on the side toward Geba, (i.e., they approached) the valley between them.

notes.334: (tn): Or “the servant who was carrying his military equipment” (likewise in vv. 6, 7, 12, 13, 14).

rashi.heb:
*מעבר הלז.* 
כל 'הלז' ו'לזה' שבמקרא, אינו לשון הזה, אלא לשון דבר שכנגדו, והוא מראהו באצבע, ובלע"ז אינו לשון ציש"ט בלע"ז, אלא ציי"ל בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *on the other side yonder.* (Heb. ‘ha-laz.’) Every ‘ha’laz’ and ‘lazeh’ in the Scriptures is not an expression of ‘ha-zeh’ (this), but it is something which is opposite the speaker, and he points it out with his finger. It is not an expression of ‘cet,’ (this), but of ‘celle’ (that) in French.

rashi.heb:
*מעבר הלז.* 
גי שני ההרים:
rashi.eng: *on the other side yonder.* of the valley between the two mountains.

rashi.heb:
*בקצה הגבעה.* 
בסוף הגבעה:
rashi.eng: *in the outskirts of Gibeah.* (Heb. ‘bik’zeh’) at the edge of Gibeah.

notes.335: (tn, Heb): “bearing.” Many English versions understand this verb to mean “wearing” (cf. KJV, NAB, NASB, NIV, NLT).

rashi.heb:
*נשא אפוד.* 
אורים ותומים:
rashi.eng: *wearing an ephod.* (This includes the ‘hoshen’ with the) urim and tummim.

rashi.heb:
*ובין המעברות אשר בקש יונתן לעבור.* 
כן היה עשוי, שן הסלע היה מהעבר מזה לבין המעברות מזה, ושן הסלע לבין המעברות מזה הגיא הוא קרוי בין המעברות, והיה לו סלע מכאן, וסלע מכאן, זה בעברו מזה, וזה בעברו מזה, והגיא בין שני העברים, אותו הגיא בקש יונתן לעבור:
rashi.eng: *And between the sides which Jonathan sought to cross.* (Thus was the layout of the terrain, lit.) Thus it was made. There was a rocky crag from this side of ‘between the sides,’ and there was a rocky crag from the other side of ‘between the sides.’ The valley is called ‘between the sides,’ and it had a stone from here and a stone from here, one on this side and one on the other side, and the valley was between the two sides. It was that valley that Jonathan sought to cross.

rashi.heb:
*שן הסלע.* 
שם שן האחד 'בוצץ', ושם השני 'סנה':
rashi.eng: *the name of one.* The name of one crag was Bozez and the name of the second was Seneh.

rashi.heb:
*מצוק מצפון.* 
משופע ועולה מצד צפון אל מכמש:
rashi.eng: *was situated from the north.* slanting from the north side toward Michmash.

rashi.heb:
*מול גבע.* 
שממנה יצא יהונתן:
rashi.eng: *opposite Geba.* whence Jonathan emerged.

notes.338: (tn, Heb): “Look, I am with you, according to your heart.” See the note at 13:14.

rashi.heb:
*דמו.* 
המתינו, כמו (יהושע י יב): שמש בגבעון דום ; וכן (תהלים לז ז): דום לה', אם כה יאמרו: דומו ונעלה אליכם, שעתם מצלחת ולבם רם עליהם:
rashi.eng: *Wait!.* (Heb. ‘domu’) Wait, like: “Sun, wait in Gibeon” (Jos. 10: 12), and so, “Wait for the Lord” (Ps. 37:7). If they say thus, “Wait, and we shall go up to you,” they are prosperous at this time, and they are proud.

rashi.heb:
*ואם כה יאמרו עלו עלינו.* 
פחד הקב"ה בלבם, ויראים לזוז ממקומם:
rashi.eng: *And if they say thus, ‘Come up to us,’ then shall we go up..* A fear inspired by the Holy One Blessed be He is in their heart, and they are afraid to move from their place.

notes.343: (tn): The perfect verbal form is used rhetorically here to express Jonathan’s certitude. As far as he is concerned, the victory is as good as won and can be described as such.

rashi.heb:
*ויענו.* 
לשון הרמת קול:
rashi.eng: *And they called.* (Heb. ‘va’ya’anu,) an expression of raising the voice.

notes.345: (tn, Heb): “and the one carrying his equipment was killing after him.”

rashi.heb:
*על ידיו ועל רגליו.* 
כלומר בכל כח ומרוצה:
rashi.eng: *on his hands and on his feet.* i.e., with all his might and running.

rashi.heb:
*כבחצי מענה צמד שדה.* 
בתוך שיעור מדת קרקע, מלא חצי מענה של מחרישת צמד בקר החורשת בשדה:
rashi.eng: *in about half a furrow, (which) a yoke (of oxen plow in) a field.* (He killed them) within the limit of a land measure, viz., the amount of half a furrow of the plowing of a yoke of oxen plowing a field.

rashi.heb:
*מענה.* 
הוא תלם המחרישה, שקורין ריי"א בלע"ז, וגבורה גדולה היא זו, שהיו קרובים זה לזה, ונכונים לעזור זה את זה:
rashi.eng: *furrow.* (Heb. ‘ma’anah’) That is the ridge which is called ‘rainure’ (ridge or furrow) in French. It was a very mighty deed, because they were close to one another and ready to aid one another.

notes.347: (tn, Heb): “and it was by the fear of God.” The translation understands this to mean that God was the source or cause of the fear experienced by the Philistines. This seems to be the most straightforward reading of the sentence. It is possible, however, that the word “God” functions here simply to intensify the accompanying word “fear,” in which one might translate “a very great fear” (cf. NAB, NRSV). It is clear that on some occasions that the divine name carries such a superlative nuance. For examples see Jo�on 2:525 �141.n.

notes.348: (tn, Heb): “at Gibeah of Benjamin.” The words “in the territory” are supplied in the translation for clarity.
notes.350: (tn, Heb): “the crowd melted and went, even here.”

rashi.heb:
*הצופים לשאול.* 
הצופים אשר היו לשאול בגבעת בנימן, צופים ; אישקאגט"ש בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *Saul’s lookouts.* the lookouts whom Saul had in Gibeah of Benjamin. Lookouts (Heb. ‘zophim’) ‘esculca’ in Old French.

rashi.heb:
*והנה ההמון.* 
של פלשתים, נמוג ממקומו וילך, וקרב הלום לצד ישראל:
rashi.eng: *and behold the multitude.* of the Philistines wandered from its place and continuously came nearer to there, to the side of the Israelites.

rashi.heb:
*נמוג.* 
כמו (בראשית ד יב): נד ונע:
rashi.eng: *wandering.* Like ‘wandering and moving.’

notes.351: (tn, Heb): “and they mustered the troops, and look!”

rashi.heb:
*פקדו.* 
לשון פקידה, כמו (איוב ז יח): ותפקדנו לבקרים:
rashi.eng: *Inspect.* An expression of supervision, like “And should inspect him every morning” (Job 7:18).

notes.352: (tc, Heb): “the ark of God.” It seems unlikely that Saul would call for the ark, which was several miles away in Kiriath-jearim (see 1 Sam 7:2). The LXX and an Old Latin ms have “ephod” here, a reading which harmonizes better with v. 3 and fits better with the verb “bring near” (see 1 Sam 23:9; 30:7) and with the expression “withdraw your hand” in v.19. This reading is followed in the present translation (cf. NAB, TEV, NLT).
notes.353: (tc, Heb): “for the ark of God was in that day, and the sons of Israel.” The translation follows the text of some Greek manuscripts. See the previous note.

rashi.heb:
*הגישה ארון האלהים.* 
אורים ותומים:
rashi.eng: *Bring near the Ark of God.* Urim and Tummim.

rashi.heb:
*כי היה ארון האלהים ביום ההוא.* 
המקרא חסר תיבה אחת, כי היה ארון האלהים שם ביום ההוא:
rashi.eng: *for the Ark of God was on that day.* This verse is missing one word: for the Ark of God was there on that day.

notes.356: (tn, Heb): “the sword of a man against his companion, a very great panic.”

notes.357: (tn, Heb): “and the Hebrews were to the Philistines formerly, who went up with them in the camp all around.”

rashi.heb:
*והעברים היו לפלשתים.* 
בעזרתם, מחמת יראה מתמול שלשום, והיום נהפכו גם המה עם חבריהם, להיות בעזרת אחיהם:
rashi.eng: *And the Hebrews (who) were with the Philistines.* at their aid out of fear, in earlier times, today they too turned with their fellows to be at the assistance of their brethren.

notes.358: (tc): The LXX includes the following words: “And all the people were with Saul, about ten thousand men. And the battle extended to the entire city on mount Ephraim.”

rashi.heb:
*נגש ביום ההוא.* 
היו אצים ונגושים להלחם בפלשתים:
rashi.eng: *And the men of Israel were hard pressed.* They were being rushed and pressed to wage war against the Philistines.

rashi.heb:
*ויואל.* 
לשון אלה:
rashi.eng: *adjured.* (Heb. ‘va’yo’el.’) an expression of an oath.

rashi.heb:
*אשר יאכל לחם.* 
כל מאכל במשמע, כמו (ירמיהו יא יט): נשחיתה עץ בלחמו:
rashi.eng: *who will eat food.* (Heb. ‘lehem,’ lit. bread) All food is included in the meaning of this word, like “Let us destroy the tree with its fruit.” (Heb. ‘b’lahmo’) (Jer. 11:19).

rashi.heb:
*ויהי דבש.* 
דבש קנים גדל בארץ ישראל:
rashi.eng: *and there was honey.* Cane sugar grows in Eretz Israel.

notes.361: (tn, Heb): “and the army entered the forest, and look!”
notes.362: (tn, Heb): “and there was no one putting his hand to his mouth.”

rashi.heb:
*והנה הלך דבש.* 
שהיה נוטף מן הקנים:
rashi.eng: *a flow of honey.* which was flowing from the canes.

notes.363: (tn, Heb): “and he returned his hand to his mouth.”
notes.364: (tc): The translation follows the Qere and several medieval Hebrew mss in reading “gleamed,” rather than the Kethib, “saw.”

rashi.heb:
*ביערת הדבש.* 
בקנה הדבש, כמו (שמות ב ג): ותשם בסוף, דמתרגמינן: ושויתיה ביערא. ו'סוף' הם קנים של אגם, וכן (שיר השירים ה א): אכלתי יערי עם דבשי. ובלשון ישמעאל קורין לאותו דבש סוקר"א בלע"ז, מפי רבי נתן הישמעאלי:
rashi.eng: *into the honeycomb..* (Heb. ‘ya’rath D’vash,’ lit. the forest of honey.) into the sugar cane, like “and she placed it in the reeds” (Exod. 2:3) which Onkelos renders: and she placed it in the ‘yaar,’ and reeds are grasses which grow in the swamp. (Hence, we find that a group or clump of grasses or canes, may be referred to as ‘yaar.’) And so, “I ate my sugar cane with my sugar,” (S. of S. 5:1), and in Arabic, that honey is called ‘sukra’ in their language. (sic) From Rabbi Nathan the Ishmaelite.

notes.365: (tn, Heb): “your father surely put the army under an oath.” The infinitive absolute is used before the finite verb to emphasize the solemn nature of the oath.

rashi.heb:
*עכר אבי את הארץ.* 
בלבל את דעתם ואת ישועתם, כמים עכורים:
rashi.eng: *My father has perturbed the land.* (Heb. ‘achar’) He confused their thoughts, and (hindered) their salvation, like unclear water (‘maim 'achurim’).

rashi.heb:
*כי עתה לא רבתה מכה.* 
בתמיה:
rashi.eng: *would there not now have been a greater slaughter among the Philistines?.* This is a question.

notes.367: (tc): The translation follows the Qere and many medieval Hebrew mss in reading “and they rushed greedily upon,” rather than the Kethib, “and they did.”
notes.368: (tc): The translation reads with the Qere and many medieval Hebrew mss הַשָּׁלָל (hashalal, “the spoil”) rather than following the Kethib reading, שָׁלָל (shalal, “spoil”).

rashi.heb:
*ויעש העם.* 
כמו ויעט העם, לשון עיט (בראשית טו יא):
rashi.eng: *And the people flew.* (Heb. ‘va’ya’at,’) similar to ‘va’yo’at bahem’ (infra 25:14) “and he drove them away (He made them fly),” an expression of ‘ayit’ (birds of prey) who swoop down on their victims (Gen. 15:11).

rashi.heb:
*צאן ובקר ובני בקר.* 
אומר אני: זה אותו ואת בנו לא תשחטו (ויקרא כב כח), ולכך קראם חוטאים. ורבותינו אמרו בשחיטת קדשים, שהיו מקדישים אותם שלמים, ואוכלים לפני זריקת דם, הוא שאמר: ויאכל העם על הדם, אוכלים קדשים ועדיין דם במזרק:
rashi.eng: *sheep, and oxen, and calves.* (lit., oxen and young of oxen) I say that this was a violation of the precept: You must not slaughter it and its young on the same day (Lev. 22:28). He, therefore, called them sinners (infra v. 33). But our Rabbis said in Tractate Zebahim (120a) that they sanctified them for peace-offerings, and they were eating before the sprinkling of the blood. This is what the Scripture means when it states: “And the people ate with the blood,” they ate when the blood was yet in the basin.

notes.369: (tn, Heb): “You have acted deceptively.” In this context the verb refers to violating an agreement, in this case the dietary and sacrificial regulations of the Mosaic law. The verb form is second masculine plural; apparently Saul here addresses those who are eating the animals.

rashi.heb:
*גלו אלי.* 
לשון גללו:
rashi.eng: *Roll to me.* (Heb. ‘golu’) like ‘gil’lu.’

rashi.heb:
*היום.* 
מבעוד יום, ולמטה (פסוק לד) נאמר: ויגישו איש שורו בידו הלילה, רבותינו נחלקו בדבר בסוף מסכת זבחים, יש מהן פירשו: כאן בחולין כאן בקדשים. ויש מהן פירשו: כאן בקדשים שהוקדשו ליקרב בבמת נוב גדולה, כאן בקדשים שהוקדשו ליקרב בבמה קטנה, למד על עולת יחיד שכשירה לישחט בלילה:
rashi.eng: *this day.* while it is yet daytime, and below (v. 34) it is stated: and all the people brought near, each man his ox in his hand that night. 0ur Rabbis at the end of Tractate Zebahim (120a) hold diverse views. Some of them explain: Here (v. 34) (the Scripture is referring to) ordinary animals, while here (v. 33) (the Scripture is referring to) sacrificial animals. Others explained: Here (v. 33) (the Scripture is referring to) sacrificial animals which were sanctified to be offered at the large high place in Nob, while here (v. 34) (the Scripture is referring to) sacrificial animals which were sanctified to be offered at a small high place. The Scripture thereby teaches us that a private burnt offering may be slaughtered at night (in a small, or private high place).

rashi.heb:
*אבן גדולה.* 
עשאה במה, לזרוק עליה דם והקטר חלבים:
rashi.eng: *a huge stone.* He made it a high place to sprinkle the blood thereon and for burning the fatty parts.

notes.370: (tn, Heb): “and all the army brought near, each his ox by his hand, and they slaughtered there.”

rashi.heb:
*פוצו בעם.* 
הכריזו במקומות הרבה, ויהיו המכריזים נפוצים בעם:
rashi.eng: *Disperse among the people.* Announce in many places, and let the announcers disperse among the people.

rashi.heb:
*ושחטתם בזה.* 
כאן, במקום שחיטה דבר אחר: סכין בדק להם:
rashi.eng: *and you shall slaughter here..* (Heb. ‘bazeh,’ lit. ‘in this’ or ‘with this’) Here is the place of slaughtering. Another explanation is: He examined a slaughtering knife for them.

rashi.heb:
*הלילה.* 
בהמות של חולין נשחטו בלילה, כך מפורש בזבחים (שם):
rashi.eng: *that night.* The ordinary animals were slaughtered at night. Thus it is explained in Zeb.

rashi.heb:
*אותו החל.* 
אותו המזבח, ראשון למזבחות שבנה שאול:
rashi.eng: *with that one he started.* That altar was the first of the altars which Saul built.

notes.372: (tn, Heb): “until the light of the morning.”
notes.373: (tn, Heb): “and there will not be left among them a man.”
notes.374: (tn, Heb): “all that is good in your eyes.” So also in v. 40.

rashi.heb:
*פנות העם.* 
שרי העם, אבן הפנה היא החשובה:
rashi.eng: *you chiefs of the people.* (lit., the corners of the people) i.e., the chiefs of the people. The cornerstone is the most esteemed.

notes.376: (tn, Heb): “and there was no one answering from all the army.”

rashi.heb:
*לעבר אחד.* 
להפיל גורל בין כלכם ובינינו:
rashi.eng: *to one side.* to cast lots between all of you, and us.

notes.377: (tc, Heb): “to the Lord God of Israel: ‘Give what is perfect.’” The Hebrew textual tradition has accidentally omitted several words here. The present translation follows the LXX (as do several English versions, cf. NAB, NRSV, TEV). See P. K. McCarter, I Samuel (AB), 247-48, and R. W. Klein, 1 Samuel (WBC), 132. The Urim and Thummim were used for lot casting in ancient Israel. Their exact identity is uncertain; they may have been specially marked stones drawn from a bag. See Exod 28:30; Lev 8:8, and Deut 33:8, as well as the discussion in R. W. Klein, 1 Samuel (WBC), 140.

rashi.heb:
*הבה תמים.* 
תן גורל אמת:
rashi.eng: *Give a perfect lot.* Give a true lot.

rashi.heb:
*והעם יצאו.* 
נקיים מן הגורל:
rashi.eng: *and the people escaped.* innocent, from the lot.

notes.379: (tc): The LXX includes the following words: “Whomever the Lord will indicate by the lot, let him die! And the people said to Saul, ‘It is not this word.’ But Saul prevailed over the people, and they cast lots between him and between Jonathan his son.”

notes.380: (tn, Heb): “Look, I, I will die.” Apparently Jonathan is acquiescing to his anticipated fate of death. However, the words may be taken as sarcastic (“Here I am about to die!”) or as a question, “Must I now die?” (cf. NAB, NIV, NCV, NLT).

notes.381: (tn, Heb): “So God will do and so he will add, surely you will certainly die, Jonathan.”

rashi.heb:
*ויפדו העם.* 
התירו לו לשאול שבועתו:
rashi.eng: *and the people redeemed Jonathan.* They nullified Saul’s oath for him.

notes.384: (tn, Heb): “his,” which could refer to Israel or to Saul.
notes.385: (tc): The translation follows the LXX (“he was delivered”), rather than the MT, which reads, “he acted wickedly.”

rashi.heb:
*ויעש חיל.* 
ויאסף חיל:
rashi.eng: *ויעש חיל.* And he gathered an army.

notes.387: (sn): The list differs from others. In 1 Sam 31:2 (= 1 Chr 10:2), Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malki-Shua are listed as Saul’s sons, while 1 Chr 8:33 and 9:39 list Jonathan, Malki-Shua, Abinadab, and Eshbaal.

notes.388: (sn): The word “uncle” can modify either Abner or Ner. See the note on the word “son” in v. 51 for further discussion.

rashi.heb:
*אבינר בן נר.* 
ונר היה דוד שאול, אחיו של קיש, ושניהם בני אביאל, וגם אביאל נקרא נר, בדברי הימים (א ח לג), שהיה מדליק נרות לרבים במבואות האפלים (ויקרא רבה ט ב):
rashi.eng: *Abner the son of Ner.* And Ner was Saul’s uncle, the brother of Kish, and they were both the sons of Abiel. Abiel was also known as Ner, in (I) Chron. (8:33), because he would light candles for the public in the dark streets.

notes.389: (tn): 1 Chr 9:35-36 indicates that Jeiel (= Abiel?) had two sons (among others) named Ner and Kish (see also 1 Sam 9:1 and 1 Chr 8:30, where some Greek manuscripts include the name Ner, though it is absent in the Hebrew text). If this Kish was the father of Saul and Ner was the father of Abner, then Saul and Abner were cousins. However, according to 1 Chr 8:33 and 9:39, Ner, not Abiel, was the father of Kish. In this case, Kish and Abner were brothers and Abner was Saul’s uncle. The simplest solution to the problem is to see two men named Kish in the genealogy: Abiel (Jeiel) was the father of Ner and Kish I. Ner was the father of Abner and Kish II. Kish II was the father of Saul. The Kish mentioned in 1 Sam 9:1 was the father of Saul (v.2) and must be identified as Kish II. In this case the genealogy is “gapped,” with Ner being omitted. Abiel was the grandfather of Kish II.

rashi.heb:
*וראה שאול.* 
לשון הוה, כשהיה שאול רואה איש גבור חיל, היה אוספו אליו:
rashi.eng: *And when Saul would see.* This is a present tense, meaning: And when Saul would see a valiant soldier, he would bring him in to himself.

notes.390: (tn, Heb): “to the voice of the words of the Lord” (so KJV).

rashi.heb:
*ועתה שמע לקול דברי ה'.* 
פעם אחת נסכלת, עתה הזהר בעצמך:
rashi.eng: *and now, hearken to the voice of the words of the Lord.* Once you acted foolishly. Now, take heed.

notes.391: (tn, Heb): “what Amalek did to Israel, how he placed against him.”
notes.392: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Israel) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

notes.393: (tn): Or perhaps “don’t take pity on” (cf. CEV).

rashi.heb:
*משור ועד שה.* 
שהיו בעלי כשפים, ומשנין עצמן ודומין לבהמה:
rashi.eng: *ox and sheep.* for they were sorcerers, and they would change themselves to resemble animals.

rashi.heb:
*וישמע שאול.* 
לשון הכרזה, כמו (לעיל יד כ): ויזעק שאול:
rashi.eng: *And Saul called… together.* An expression of announcing, as though it would say, שאול ויזעק.

rashi.heb:
*ויפקדם בטלאים.* 
אמר לכל אחד ואחד, שיקח טלה מצאנו של מלך, ואחר כך מנה את הטלאים, לפי שאסור למנות את ישראל, שנאמר בם (בראשית לב יב): לא יספר מרוב:
rashi.eng: *and he counted them in Telaim.* (According to ‘peshat,’ this is the name of a place, as in Jos. 15:24. Our Rabbis, however, take it as a common noun, meaning ‘with lambs,’ explaining thus:) He told everyone to take a lamb from the King’s flocks, since it is forbidden to count Jews, for it is stated concerning them: “which will not be counted for multitude” (Gen. 32:12).

notes.396: (tc): The LXX has the plural here, “cities.”
notes.397: (tc): The translation follows the LXX and Vulgate which assume a reading וַיָּאָרֶב (vayya’arev, “and he set an ambush,” from the root ארב [’rv] with quiescence of alef) rather than the MT, which has וַיָּרֶב (vayyareb, “and he contended,” from the root ריב [ryv]).

rashi.heb:
*וירב בנחל.* 
וילחם בנחל ורבותינו אמרו (יומא כב ב): על עסקי נחל רב ודן את עצמו, ומה בשביל נפש אחת אמרה תורה ערוף עגלה בנחל, בשביל כל הנפשות האלו לא כל שכן, אם אדם חטא, בהמה מה חטאה:
rashi.eng: *and he fought in the valley.* (וירב) and he fought in the valley (from ריב, a quarrel). Our Rabbis said: Concerning the valley, he argued and concluded, thus: if for the sake of one soul, the Torah said, “decapitate a calf in the valley” (Deut. 21), how much more for the sake of all these souls. If man has sinned, what have the animals sinned?

notes.399: (tc): The translation follows the Syriac Peshitta and Vulgate which assume a reading אֶסִפְךָ (’esf�ka, “I sweep you away,” from the root ספה [sfh]) rather than the MT אֹסִפְךָ (’osif�ka, “I am gathering you,” from the root אסף[’sf]).

rashi.heb:
*אל הקיני.* 
בני יתרו, שהיו יושבין במדבר יהודה בנגב ערד, שהלכו אצל יעבץ ללמוד תורה, וערד הוא עמלק, הכנעני מלך ערד, עמלק היה, שנאמר (במדבר כא א): יושב הנגב, ועמלק יושב בארץ הנגב (שם יג כט):
rashi.eng: *to the Kenites.* the descendants of Jethro, who were residing in the wilderness of Judea, in the south of Arad, who went to Jabez to learn Torah, Arad being Amalek. The Canaanite king of Arad was Amalek, for it is stated: “the dweller of the South” (Num. 21:1), and “Amalek dwells in the Southland” (ibid. 12:29).

rashi.heb:
*עם כל בני ישראל.* 
שנהנו מסעודתו משה ואהרן וכל זקני ישראל, והרי מעלה עליו כאלו עשה חסד עם כל בני ישראל:
rashi.eng: *with all the children of Israel.* for Moses, Aaron, and all the elders of Israel partook of his (Jethro’s) repast (Ex. 18:12). (The Scripture, therefore) considers it as though he had done kindness with all the children of Israel.

notes.401: (tn, Heb): “all the people.” For clarity “Agag’s” has been supplied in the translation.

notes.402: (tn): The Hebrew text is difficult here. We should probably read וְהַמַּשְׂמַנִּים (v�hammasmannim, “the fat ones”) rather than the MT וְהַמִּשְׂנִים (v�hammisnim, “the second ones”). However, if the MT is retained, the sense may be as the Jewish commentator Kimchi supposed: the second-born young, thought to be better than the firstlings. (For discussion see S. R. Driver, Notes on the Hebrew Text and the Topography of the Books of Samuel, 123-24.)
notes.404: (tc): The MT has here the very odd form נְמִבְזָה (n�mivzah), but this is apparently due to a scribal error. The translation follows instead the Niphal participle נִבְזָה (nivzah).

rashi.heb:
*והמשנים.* 
אין לו דמיון, והם הבריאים ואומר אני: לשון 'משנים', כמו (בראשית מג יב): כסף משנה, על שם שהוא כפול בבשר ובשומן, וכן (שופטים ו כה): ופר השני שבע שנים:
rashi.eng: *and the fatlings.* (Heb. ‘vehamishnim.’) It has no likeness (to any other word in the Scriptures). These are the fatlings, and I say that the expression of ‘mishnim’ is like ‘kesef mishneh’ (double money Gen. 43:15) because they are doubled over with flesh and fat. Similarly, (we explain:) “And the ox which was fattened (sheni) seven years.” (Jud. 6:25).

rashi.heb:
*נמבזה ונמס.* 
כמו נבזה, והמ"ם טפילה בו:
rashi.eng: *vile and feeble.* (נמבזה) like נבזה (despised), and the ‘mem’ is superfluous.

rashi.heb:
*נחמתי.* 
מחשבה עלתה בלבי על מלכות שאול שהמלכתי:
rashi.eng: *I regret.* A thought has arisen in my heart concerning the kingdom of Saul, whom I have appointed king.

notes.406: (tn, Heb): “and he turned and crossed over.”
notes.407: (tc): At the end of v. 12 the LXX and one Old Latin ms include the following words not found in the MT: “to Saul. And behold, he was offering as a burnt offering to the Lord the best of the spoils that he had brought from the Amalekites.”

rashi.heb:
*מציב לו יד.* 
בונה לו מזבח הוא המזבח שנאמר באליהו (מלכים-א יח ל): וירפא את מזבח ה' ההרוס. ויונתן תרגם: והא מתקן ליה תמן אתר לפלגא ביה ביזתא:
rashi.eng: *he is setting up a place for himself.* He is building an altar for himself. That is the altar referred to concerning Elijah, “And he repaired the altar of the Lord, which had been torn down.” Jonathan however, renders: and behold, he is setting up there a place for himself, to divide the spoils.

notes.409: (tn): The words “if that is the case” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.

notes.412: (tc, Heb): The translation follows the Qere and many medieval Hebrew mss in reading the singular (“he said”) rather than the plural (“they said”) of the Kethib. “he”; the referent (Saul) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*הרף.* 
כתרגומו: אוריך, פירוש המתן:
rashi.eng: *Desist.* Like the Targum, ‘orich,’ meaning ‘wait’.

rashi.heb:
*ראש שבטי ישראל אתה.* 
תרגם יונתן: שבטא דבנימין עבר בימא בריש כל עמא, כמה שנאמר (תהלים סח כח): בנימין צעיר רודם:
rashi.eng: *are you not the head of the tribes of Israel.* Jonathan renders: The tribe of Benjamin crossed the Reed Sea at the head of the people, as it is said: “Benjamin, the youngest, rules over them” (Ps. 68: 28).

notes.415: (tc): The translation follows the LXX, the Syriac Peshitta, and the Targum in reading the second person singular suffix (“you”) rather than the third person plural suffix of the MT (“they”).

rashi.heb:
*עד כלותם אותם.* 
העם אשר אתך יכלו אותם:
rashi.eng: *until they destroy them.* The people who are with you will destroy them.

notes.416: (tn, Heb): “listened to the voice of the Lord.”
notes.417: (tn, Heb): “you have done what is evil in the eyes of the Lord.”

rashi.heb:
*ותעט.* 
כמו ותעף, לשון עיט (בראשית טו יא):
rashi.eng: *but you flew.* (ותעט,) like ותעף (and you flew), an expression relating to עיט, bird of prey (Gen. 15:11).

notes.418: (tn, Heb): “listened to the voice of the Lord.”

rashi.heb:
*ראשית החרם.* 
מיטב החרם, וכן (דברים יח ד): ראשית דגנך, כמה שנאמר (במדבר יח ל): בהרימכם את חלבו ממנו. ויונתן תרגם: קדם דיחרמון:
rashi.eng: *the best of the ban.* (ראשית, lit., the beginning), and similarly, “the best of your corn” (Deut. 18: 4), as it is said: “When you separate the best part of it therefrom” (Num. 18:30). Jonathan however, renders: before they banned it.

notes.420: (tn, Heb): “as [in] listening to the voice of the Lord.”
notes.423: (tn): The expression “is better” is understood here by ellipsis (see the immediately preceding statement).

rashi.heb:
*הנה שמוע.* 
בקולו, טוב מזבח:
rashi.eng: *Behold, to obey.* His command is better than a peace-offering.

rashi.heb:
*להקשיב מחלב אילים.* 
זה מוסב על הנה שמוע מזבח טוב, ולהקשיב, מחלב אילים:
rashi.eng: *to hearken, than the fat of rams..* This refers to: Behold, to obey is better than a peace- offering, and to hearken (is better) than the fat of rams.

rashi.heb:
*כי חטאת קסם מרי ואון ותרפים הפצר.* 
וכעונש של און ותרפים, כן עונש של הפצר ויונתן תרגם: ארי כחוב גבריא וכו' וכחובי עמא דטעו בתר טעותא, כן חובת כל אנש דפצר ומוסיף וכו':
rashi.eng: *For rebellion is as the sin of divination, and stubbornness is as idolatry and teraphim.* And like the penalty for idolatry and teraphim, so is the penalty for stubbornness. Jonathan renders: for, as the sin of a people who divine, so is the sin of any man who disobeys the word of the Lord; and as the sins of a nation who has strayed after idols, so is the sin of any person who adds to the words of a prophet.

rashi.heb:
*הפצר.* 
לשון תוספת, וכן (בראשית לג יא): ויפצר בו, הרבה עליו דברים:
rashi.eng: *stubbornness.* An expression of adding, and similarly, (Gen. 36:11) He prevailed upon him (ויפצר). He spoke many words to convince him.

notes.427: (tn, Heb): “and I listened to their voice.”

rashi.heb:
*יראתי את העם.* 
דואג האדומי, שהיה חשוב כולם:
rashi.eng: *I feared the people.* Doeg the Edomite, who was as esteemed as all of them.

notes.428: (tn): Following the imperative, the cohortative with the prefixed conjunction indicates purpose/result.

notes.429: (tn, Heb): “he,” but Saul is clearly the referent. A Qumran ms and the LXX include the name “Saul” here.

rashi.heb:
*ויחזק בכנף מעילו.* 
לפי פשוטו משמעו, שכשפנה שמואל ללכת מאחרי שאול, אחז שאול בכנף של שמואל, לפי שהיה שאול מבקש ממנו שישוב עד שישתחוה בגלגל שהיה שם אהל מועד ומדרש אגדה (שוחר טוב) חולקים אמוראים, יש אומרים: מעילו של שמואל קרע שאול. ויש אומרים: מעילו של שאול קרע שמואל, ומסר לו סימן זה, מי שיכרות כנף מעילו, הוא ימלוך תחתיו, והוא שאמר לו שאול לדוד ביום שכרת את המעיל (לקמן כד כ): ידעתי כי מלוך תמלוך:
rashi.eng: *and he seized the skirt of his robe.* According to the simple interpretation, the implication is that when Samuel turned to go away from following Saul, Saul seized the skirt of Samuel’s robe, since Saul was entreating him to return until he would prostrate himself in Gilgal, where the tent of meeting had been. In Midrash Aggadah, however, Amoraim differ on this point. Some say that Saul tore Samuel’s robe, and some say that Samuel tore Saul’s robe, thereby giving over to him this sign, that whoever would sever the skirt of his robe would reign in his place. And that is what Saul said to David on the day that he severed the robe, “I know that you will reign” (infra 24:21).

notes.430: (tn, Heb): “splendor,” used here by metonymy as a title for the Lord.
notes.432: (sn): This observation marks the preceding statement (v. 28) as an unconditional, unalterable decree. When God makes such a decree he will not alter it or change his mind. This does not mean that God never deviates from his stated intentions or changes his mind. On the contrary, several passages describe him as changing his mind. In fact, his willingness to do so is one of his fundamental divine attributes (see Joel 2:13; Jonah 4:2). For a fuller discussion see R. B. Chisholm, Jr., “Does God Change His Mind?” BSac 152 (1995): 387-99.

rashi.heb:
*וגם נצח ישראל לא ישקר.* 
ואם תאמר אשוב מעוני לפניו, לא יועיל עוד ליטול את המלוכה ממי שנתנה לו, כי הקב"ה שהוא נצחונו של ישראל, לא ישקר מליתן הטובה לזה שאמר ליתן:
rashi.eng: *And also, the Strength of Israel will neither lie.* And if you say, “I shall repent of my sin before Him, it will no longer avail to take the kingdom from the one to whom it was given, for the Holy One, Blessed be He, Who is the Strength of Israel, will not lie by not giving the good to whom He promised to give it.”

notes.433: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Saul) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

notes.434: (tn): The MT reading מַעֲדַנֹּת (ma’adannot, literally, “bonds,” used here adverbially, “in bonds”) is difficult. The word is found only here and in Job 38:31. Part of the problem lies in determining the root of the word. Some scholars have taken it to be from the root ענד (’nd, “to bind around”), but this assumes a metathesis of two of the letters of the root. Others take it from the root עדן (’dn) with the meaning “voluptuously,” but this does not seem to fit the context. It seems better to understand the word to be from the root מעד (m’d, “to totter” or “shake”). In that case it describes the fear that Agag experienced in realizing the mortal danger that he faced as he approached Samuel. This is the way that the LXX translators understood the word, rendering it by the Greek participle τρέμον (tremon, “trembling”).
notes.436: (tc): The text is difficult here. With the LXX, two Old Latin mss, and the Syriac Peshitta it is probably preferable to delete סָר (sar, “is past”) of the MT; it looks suspiciously like a dittograph of the following word מַר (mar, “bitter”). This further affects the interpretation of Agag’s comment. In the MT he comes to Samuel confidently assured that the danger is over (cf. KJV, NASB, NIV “Surely the bitterness of death is past,” along with NLT, CEV). However, it seems more likely that Agag realized that his fortunes had suddenly taken a turn for the worse and that the clemency he had enjoyed from Saul would not be his lot from Samuel. The present translation thus understands Agag to approach not confidently but in the stark realization that his death is imminent (“Surely death is bitter!”). Cf. NAB “So it is bitter death!”; NRSV “Surely this is the bitterness of death”; TEV “What a bitter thing it is to die!”

rashi.heb:
*אגג מעדנות.* 
יונתן תרגם: אגג מפנקא:
rashi.eng: *And Agag went to him delicately.* (Heb. ‘ma’adanoth.’) Jonathan renders: delicately.

rashi.heb:
*אכן סר מר המות.* 
באמת ידעתי כי סר וקרב עלי מרירת המות:
rashi.eng: *Surely, the bitterness of death has turned..* Indeed, I know that the bitterness of death has turned toward me, and is approaching.

rashi.heb:
*כאשר שכלה נשים חרבך.* 
להושיבם אלמנות מבעליהם, שהייתם חותכים זנבי בחורי ישראל:
rashi.eng: *As your sword bereaved women.* to render them veritable widows from their husbands, for you would cut off the membrum virile of the youths of Israel.

rashi.heb:
*וישסף.* 
חתכו לארבע, ואין לתיבה זו דמיון ותרגום וישסף, ופשח. ובגמרא שלנו יש הוה מפשח ויהיב לן אלותא, כלומר בוקע:
rashi.eng: *And he hewed.* (וישסף) He cut him into four pieces. There is no similarity to this word. The Targum renders: ‘ufashah.’ And in our Gemara (i.e., T.B., Bets. 33b) we find: He broke a branch off (‘m’fashah’), and gave us each several sticks, meaning that he split.

notes.438: (tc): The Lucianic recension of the Old Greek translation includes the following words: “And the Lord said to Samuel.”
notes.439: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map7-E2; Map8-E2; Map10-B4.
notes.440: (tn, Heb): “for I have seen among his sons for me a king.”

rashi.heb:
*בית הלחמי.* 
בבית לחם, וכן דרך כל דבר ששמו בשתי תיבות, כמו: בית לחם, בית שמש, בית אל, קרית ארבע, אם בא להטיל בו ה"א, מטיל בין שתי התיבות, כגון: קרית הארבע, בית האלי, בית הלחמי:
rashi.eng: *the Bethlehemite.* (בית-הלחמי,) from Bethlehem, and so is the rule of every noun which is composed of two words, e.g., Beth-lehem, Beth-shemesh, Beth-el, Kiriath-arba, if one wishes to add a ‘heh’ (definite article) thereto, he adds it between the two words, e.g., Kiriath-ha’arba (Gen. 35:27), בית-האלי (I Kings 16:34), בית-הלחמי.

notes.444: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map7-E2; Map8-E2; Map10-B4.
notes.445: (tc): In the MT the verb is singular (“he said”), but the translation follows many medieval Hebrew mss and ancient versions in reading the plural (“they said”).

rashi.heb:
*ויחרדו.* 
מהרו לצאת לקראתו:
rashi.eng: *hurried.* (lit., trembled) hurried out toward him.

notes.446: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Samuel) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.448: (tn, Heb): “said”; the words “to himself” are implied, given the secrecy surrounding Samuel’s mission to Bethlehem (v. 2).

rashi.heb:
*ויאמר אך נגד ה' משיחו.* 
ויאמר בלבו, אך אמת הוא זה:
rashi.eng: *that he said, “Surely, before the Lord is His anointed.”.* and he said to himself, “Surely, it is true that this one is fitting for the kingdom.”

notes.451: (tn, Heb): “for not that which the man sees.” The translation follows the LXX, which reads, “for not as man sees does God see.” The MT has suffered from homoioteleuton or homoioarcton. See P. K. McCarter, I Samuel (AB), 274.

rashi.heb:
*אל תבט אל מראהו.* 
אל יופי תארו:
rashi.eng: *Look not upon his appearance.* upon the beauty of his form.

rashi.heb:
*כי מאסתיהו.* 
לפי שכעסן הוא, כמה שנאמר (לקמן יז כח): ויחר אף אליאב בדוד:
rashi.eng: *for I have rejected him.* because he is an irascible person, as it is stated: “And Eliab’s wrath was kindled against David” (infra 17:29).

rashi.heb:
*כי לא אשר יראה האדם.* 
אף על פי שקראת לעצמך רואה, שאמרת לשאול (לעיל ט יט): אנכי הרואה, כאן אני מודיעך שאינך רואה:
