rashi.eng: *for it is not as man sees.* Even though you called yourself ‘seer,’ for you said to Saul, “I am the seer,” (supra 9:19), here I inform you that you do not see.

notes.453: (tn, Heb): “and caused him to pass before.”
notes.454: (tn, Heb): “he” (also in v. 9); the referent (Samuel) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*ויעבר ישי שמה.* 
הוא שמעא:
rashi.eng: *Shammah.* That is Shimeah (mentioned in II Sam. 12:3; II Chron. 2:13).

notes.456: (tn, Heb): “caused seven of his sons to pass before Samuel.” This could be taken as referring to seven sons in addition to the three mentioned before this, but 1 Sam 17:12 says Jesse had eight sons, not eleven. 1 Chr 2:13-15 lists only seven sons, including David. However, 1 Chr 27:18 mentions an additional son, named Elihu.

notes.457: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Jesse) has been specified in the translation both here and in v. 12 for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*שאר הקטן.* 
נשאר הקטן:
rashi.eng: *The youngest still remains.* (Heb. שאר, kal conj. active) This is like נשאר (remains, niph’al conj. passive).

rashi.heb:
*לא נסוב.* 
לא נשב לאכול, כל מושב סעודה קרויה הסבה:
rashi.eng: *we will not sit down.* (לא נסב) We will not sit down to eat. Every instance of sitting down to a meal is called הסבה (leaning).

notes.458: (tn, Heb): “and he sent and brought him.”

rashi.heb:
*ותצלח רוח ה'.* 
רוח גבורה:
rashi.eng: *And a spirit of the Lord passed.* a spirit of valiance.

notes.459: (tn): Or “an injurious spirit”; cf. NLT “a tormenting spirit.” The phrase need not refer to an evil, demonic spirit. The Hebrew word translated “evil” may refer to the character of the spirit or to its effect upon Saul. If the latter, another translation option might be “a mischief-making spirit.”

notes.460: (tn, Heb): “and he will play with his hand.”
notes.461: (tn, Heb): “and it will be better for you.”

rashi.heb:
*עבדיך לפניך.* 
הנה עבדיך לפניך אשר יעשו מצותיך:
rashi.eng: *your servants are before you.* Behold, your servants are before you, who will do your bidding.

notes.464: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map7-E2; Map8-E2; Map10-B4.
notes.465: (tn, Heb): “mighty man of valor and a man of war.”

rashi.heb:
*אחד מהנערים.* 
מיוחד שבהם, דואג האדומי:
rashi.eng: *one of the young men.* The special one of the young men, Doeg the Edomite.

rashi.heb:
*יודע נגן.* 
כל עצמו נתכוון להכניס עין רעה של שאול בדוד, שיתקנא בו:
rashi.eng: *who knows how to play.* With his entire essence, he intended to introduce Saul’s evil eye into David, i.e., that he envy him.

notes.471: (tn, Heb): “Let David stand before me, for he has found favor in my eyes.”

notes.472: (tn, Heb): “would turn aside from upon him.”

notes.473: (tc): The content of 1 Sam 17–18, which includes the David and Goliath story, differs considerably in the LXX as compared to the MT, suggesting that this story circulated in ancient times in more than one form. The LXX for chs. 17–18 is much shorter than the MT, lacking almost half of the material (39 of a total of 88 verses). Many scholars (e.g., McCarter, Klein) think that the shorter text of the LXX is preferable to the MT, which in their view has been expanded by incorporation of later material. Other scholars (e.g., Wellhausen, Driver) conclude that the shorter Greek text (or the Hebrew text that underlies it) reflects an attempt to harmonize certain alleged inconsistencies that appear in the longer version of the story. Given the translation characteristics of the LXX elsewhere in this section, it does not seem likely that these differences are due to deliberate omission of these verses on the part of the translator. It seems more likely that the Greek translator has faithfully rendered here a Hebrew text that itself was much shorter than the MT in these chapters. Whether or not the shorter text represented by the LXX is to be preferred over the MT in 1 Sam 17–18 is a matter over which textual scholars are divided. For a helpful discussion of the major textual issues in this unit see D. Barth�lemy, D. W. Gooding, J. Lust, and E. Tov, The Story of David and Goliath (OBO). Overall it seems preferable to stay with the MT, at least for the most part. However, the major textual differences between the LXX and the MT will be mentioned in the notes that accompany the translation so that the reader may be alert to the major problem passages.

rashi.heb:
*באפס דמים.* 
כך שם המקום:
rashi.eng: *in Ephes-dammim.* This is the name of the place.

notes.475: (tn, Heb): “the men of Israel” (so KJV, NASB); NAB, NIV, NRSV “the Israelites.”

notes.478: (tn, Heb): “the man of the space between the two [armies].” See v. 23.
notes.479: (tc, Heb): “his height was six cubits and a span” (cf. KJV, NASB, NRSV). A cubit was approximately eighteen inches, a span nine inches. So, according to the Hebrew tradition, Goliath was about nine feet, nine inches tall (cf. NIV, CEV, NLT “over nine feet”; NCV “nine feet, four inches”; TEV “nearly 3 metres”). However, some Greek witnesses, Josephus, and a manuscript of 1 Samuel from Qumran read “four cubits and a span” here, that is, about six feet, nine inches (cf. NAB “six and a half feet”). This seems more reasonable; it is likely that Goliath’s height was exaggerated as the story was retold. See P. K. McCarter, I Samuel (AB), 286, 291.

rashi.heb:
*איש הבנים.* 
גבור ליצא ממערכתו, לעמוד בין שתי המערכות:
rashi.eng: *the champion.* A hero who would emerge from his battle array, to stand between the two arrays.

notes.480: (sn): Although the exact weight of Goliath’s defensive body armor is difficult to estimate in terms of modern equivalency, it was obviously quite heavy. Driver, following Kennedy, suggests a modern equivalent of about 220 pounds (100 kg); see S. R. Driver, Notes on the Hebrew Text and the Topography of the Books of Samuel, 139. Klein, taking the shekel to be equal to .403 ounces, arrives at a somewhat smaller weight of about 126 pounds (57 kg); see R. W. Klein, 1 Samuel (WBC), 175. But by any estimate it is clear that Goliath presented himself as a formidable foe indeed.

rashi.heb:
*ושריון קשקשים.* 
כמין קשקשות דגים עשוין מברזל, נופלים על גב השריון [ ס"א נקבי השריון ], קשקשת לכל נקב:
rashi.eng: *and a coat of mail.* scales like those of fish, made of iron, spread over the coat (another version, the holes of the coat), a scale for each hole.

notes.481: (sn): Or “greaves.” These were coverings (probably lined for comfort) that extended from about the knee to the ankle, affording protection for the shins of a warrior.

rashi.heb:
*ומצחת נחשת.* 
כמין יד ברזל היוצא מן הכובע כנגד החוטים, שקורין נש"ל בלע"ז, והיתה מגעת לו עד רגליו:
rashi.eng: *greaves of copper.* a sort of copper handle, extending from the helmet, opposite the nose, called ‘nasal’ in French, and it reached the feet.

rashi.heb:
*וכידון נחשת.* 
תרגם יונתן: ומסחפא דנחשא נפיק מן קולסא ומטל בין כתפוהי. פירוש: כמין חנית נחשת בולטת מן הכובע, ונמשכת בין כתפיו, להגן על צוארו מן החרב:
rashi.eng: *and a copper javelin.* Jonathan renders: ומסחפא דנחשא נפיק מן קולסא ומטל בין כתפוהי A sort of copper javelin, protruding from the helmet, and extending between his shoulders, to protect his neck from the sword.

notes.482: (tn): The translation follows the Qere and many medieval Hebrew mss in reading “wood,” rather than the “arrow” (the reading of the Kethib).
notes.483: (sn): That is, about fifteen or sixteen pounds.

rashi.heb:
*כמנור אורגים.* 
תרגם יונתן כאכסן דגרדאין, אינשובל"א בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *כמנור אורגים.* like a weaver’s beam - (Jonathan) ‘ensouple’ in French (cylinder in a loom).

rashi.heb:
*שש מאות שקלים.* 
כל השקלים האמורים בנביאים, מנים:
rashi.eng: *six hundred shekels.* All shekels mentioned in the Prophetic books, are ‘maneh’s’.

notes.484: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Goliath) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.485: (tn): The Hebrew text adds “and said to them.”
notes.486: (tc): The translation follows the ancient versions in reading “choose,” (from the root בחר, bkhr), rather than the MT. The verb in MT (ברה, brh) elsewhere means “to eat food”; the sense of “to choose,” required here by the context, is not attested for this root. The MT apparently reflects an early scribal error.
notes.487: (tn): Following the imperative, the prefixed verbal form (either an imperfect or jussive) with the prefixed conjunction indicates purpose/result here.

rashi.heb:
*למה תצאו.* 
כולכם לערוך מלחמה, ילחם אחד כנגדי בשביל כולכם, ובתנאי שהוא מפורש: אם יוכל להלחם אתי וגו':
rashi.eng: *Why should you come out.* i.e., Why should all of you come out to wage war? Let one fight against me for all of you, and on the condition which is specified: if he is able to fight with me, etc.

rashi.heb:
*הלא אנכי הפלשתי.* 
איני לא שר מאה ולא שר אלף, אלא פלשתי כאחד מן האחרים, ואף על פי שנלחמתי להם כמה מלחמות, אני הרגתי חפני ופנחס, ושביתי את הארון, ואתם נעשיתם עבדים לשאול, ולא הושיע אתכם מימיו בגבורתו:
rashi.eng: *Am I not the Philistine, and you the servants of Saul?.* I am neither a captain over a hundred, nor a captain over a thousand. I am but a Philistine like one of the others, even though I have fought many wars for them. I killed Hophni and Phinehas, and I captured the Ark. You, on the other hand, have become servants to Saul, although he never saved you with his heroism.

rashi.heb:
*ברו לכם.* 
בררו לכם:
rashi.eng: *Choose for yourselves.* (ברו לכם. The root is ברר). Hence, it is like בררו לכם, (with two ‘resh’es’).

rashi.heb:
*איש.* 
את שאול, וירד אלי:
rashi.eng: *a man.* Saul, and let him come down to me.

notes.488: (tn): Following the imperative, the cohortative verbal form indicates purpose/result here.

notes.490: (tc): Some mss of the LXX lack vv. 12-31.
notes.491: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map7-E2; Map8-E2; Map10-B4.
notes.492: (tc): The translation follows the Lucianic recension of the LXX and the Syriac Peshitta in reading “in years,” rather than MT “among men.”

rashi.heb:
*אפרתי.* 
בית לחם יושבת בארץ אפרת:
rashi.eng: *And David was the son of this Ephrathite man.* Bethlehem is situated in the land of Ephrath.

rashi.heb:
*ולו שמנה בנים.* 
ומה שכתוב (בדברי הימים א ב טו): 'אוצם הששי דוד השביעי' ולא כתב יותר, יש לומר שאחד מת בלא בנים, ולפיכך לא כתבו שם:
rashi.eng: *and he had eight sons.* And that which is stated (in I Chron. 2:15), “Ozem the sixth, David the seventh,” and he states no more, may be reconciled by supposing that one died without children. He was, therefore, not counted there.

rashi.heb:
*באנשים.* 
נמנה בכנסיות החשובים:
rashi.eng: *among men.* counted in the assemblies of the esteemed men.

rashi.heb:
*ודוד הוא הקטן.* 
שהיה בבית שאול מקודם לכן לנגן לפניו:
rashi.eng: *And David was the youngest.* who had heretofore been in Saul’s palace to play music before him.

rashi.heb:
*ודוד הולך.* 
היה הולך ושב תמיד מאצל שאול לבית אביו:
rashi.eng: *Now David went.* would always go to and fro from Saul to his father’s house.

rashi.heb:
*השכם והערב.* 
אמרו רבותינו (סוטה מב ב): כדי לבטלם מקריאת שמע:
rashi.eng: *morning and evening.* Our Rabbis said: (He did this) in order to prevent them from reciting ‘Shema.’

notes.497: (tn, Heb): “and your brothers, observe with respect to welfare.”
notes.498: (tn, Heb): “and their pledge take.” This probably refers to some type of confirmation that the goods arrived safely. See R. W. Klein, 1 Samuel (WBC), 177. Cf. NIV “bring back some assurance”; NCV “some proof to show me they are all right”; NLT “bring me back a letter from them.”

rashi.heb:
*חריצי החלב.* 
(תרגום:) גובנין דחלבא:
rashi.eng: *חריצי החלב.* cheeses (Jonathan).

rashi.heb:
*לשר האלף.* 
אני אומר: לשר של אותו אלף שאחיו (ס"א שאני) ממנו, שלכל השבטים היו שרי אלפים לפי אלפיהם, ואני שמעתי: לשר האלף זה יהונתן, שאמר עליו (לעיל יג ב): ואלף היו עם יונתן בגבעת בנימין:
rashi.eng: *to the captain of the thousand.* I say (that Jesse meant) “to the captain of that thousand to which I belong,” for all the tribes had captains of thousands “according to their thousands” (This last phrase is vague). I have heard, however, that ‘to the captain of the thousand’ refers to Jonathan, concerning whom the Scripture states: “And a thousand were with Jonathan in Gibeah of Benjamin.” (supra 13:3).

rashi.heb:
*ואת ערובתם תקח.* 
ואת ערובת הצלתם ושלומם, תקח באזניך ובלבבך, ותגד לי וכן תרגם יונתן: וית טיביהון תייתי:
rashi.eng: *and the tidings of their welfare you shall take.* And the assurance of their salvation and their welfare you shall take into your ears and your heart, and you shall relate it to me. And so did Jonathan render: ‘and their welfare.’

rashi.heb:
*ערובתם.* 
לשון הצלה, כמו (תהלים קיט קכב) ערוב עבדך לטוב, גרנטי"ש בלע"ז ורבותינו אמרו (שבת נו א): גט כריתות יקח מאתם ויביא לנשותיהם, להפריד עירוב שבינו לבינה:
rashi.eng: *their welfare.* (Heb. ‘arubatham,’) an expression of salvation, like (Ps. 119:112).“Assure your servant for good,” ‘garantir’ in French. Our Rabbis said: He should take a bill of divorcement from them, and deliver it to their wives, to break the connection between man and wife (lit., between him and her).

notes.500: (tn, Heb): “to a guard”; KJV, NASB, NRSV “with a keeper”; NIV “with a shepherd.” Since in contemporary English “guard” sounds like someone at a military installation or a prison, the present translation uses “to someone else who would watch over it.”

rashi.heb:
*המעגלה.* 
סביבות המחנה עושים מעגל, והיוצא חוץ, לפנים או לאחור, מתחייב לפנים, שמא ירוצו עליו בני מערכות האויבים, לאחור, מבקש הוא לנוס:
rashi.eng: *to the barricade.* They would form a circle around the camp, and whoever would go out of the circle, either ahead of or behind the camp, would be liable (to death); ahead, lest the men of the enemy armies attack him, and behind, since he seeks to desert.

rashi.heb:
*ותערוך ישראל.* 
מערכת ישראל:
rashi.eng: *And the Israelites… put.* (The feminine form is used, referring to) the army of Israel, (which is grammatically feminine).

rashi.heb:
*שומר הכלים.* 
של בני הצבא:
rashi.eng: *the keeper of the baggage.* of the soldiers.

rashi.heb:
*ממערות פלשתים.* 
כתיב, רבותינו דרשו (סוטה מב ב): מאה בני אדם הערו בערפה אמו, כשפירשה מאחרי רות ונעמי חמותה:
rashi.eng: *from the ranks of the Philistines.* The ‘kethib’ is ממערות פלשתים. Our Rabbis expounded the word מערות: as ממאה ערלות (from 100 foreskins) meaning that one hundred men were intimate (הערו) with his mother Orpah, when she parted with Ruth and her mother-in-law Naomi.

rashi.heb:
*יעשה חפשי.* 
מדברים האמורים במשפטי המלוכה:
rashi.eng: *and he will make his father’s house free.* from the things mentioned in the laws of the kingdom.

notes.506: (tn, Heb): “and turns aside humiliation from upon Israel.”

notes.509: (tn, Heb): “his”; the referent (David) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.510: (tn, Heb): “the anger of Eliab became hot.”

notes.513: (tn, Heb): “and spoke according to this word.”

notes.516: (tn, Heb): “Let not the heart of a man fall upon him.” The LXX reads “my lord,” instead of “a man.”

rashi.heb:
*ובא הארי ואת הדוב.* 
(תרגום:) ואתא אריא ואף דובא:
rashi.eng: *ובא הארי ואת הדוב.* and also a bear (Jonathan).

notes.517: (tc): The LXX includes here the following words not found in the MT: “Should I not go and smite him, and remove today reproach from Israel? For who is this uncircumcised one?”

rashi.heb:
*גם את הארי גם הדוב.* 
הרי אלו רבוין, ארי ושני גוריו, ודוב ושני ילדיו:
rashi.eng: *Both the lion and the bear.* These three words (גם את גם) are of inclusive nature, meaning a lion and its two whelps, and a bear and its two cubs.

notes.518: (tn): Or “Go, and may the Lord be with you” (so NASB, NCV, NRSV).

rashi.heb:
*ה' אשר הצילני מיד הארי.* 
יודע אני שלא לחנם נזדמן לי הדבר ההוא, אלא שלעתיד אני בא לידי כיוצא בה לתשועת ישראל, ואסמוך עליה ואצא וזה אחד משני צדיקים שנתן להם רמז, וחשו להשכיל לדבר, דוד ומרדכי, שנאמר (אסתר ב יא): ובכל יום ויום מרדכי מתהלך לפני חצר וגו', אמר: לא לחנם עלתה בצדקת זו שנתפסה במשכב הערל הזה, אלא שעתידה היא לעמוד לישראל ביום צרה:
rashi.eng: *The Lord Who saved me from the paw of the lion.* I know that this incident did not occur to me for naught, but as an indication that in the future, I would come through similar circumstances, to a salvation for Israel. And I shall rely upon this, and go out. And he was one of the two righteous men, to whom the Almighty gave a hint, and they took heed, to understand the matter, viz., David and Mordecai, as it is stated: “And everyday, Mordecai would walk before the courtyard, etc.” (Es. 2:11) He said, “It is not for nothing that this righteous woman (Esther) has been taken into the bed of this uncircumcised one (Ahasuerus). It can only mean that she is destined to stand up for the Jews in a day of distress.”

rashi.heb:
*את דוד מדיו.* 
נהפכו להיות כמדת דוד משנמשח בשמן המשחה, אף שהיו של שאול שהיה גבוה מכל העם משכמו ומעלה (לעיל ט ב), וכיון שראה שאול כן, הכניס בו עין הרע, והרגיש דוד בדבר:
rashi.eng: *David with his garments.* They changed to David’s size, (explaining מדיו from מדה, a measure, cf., Lev. 6:3) since he had been anointed with the anointing oil, although they belonged to Saul who was taller than any of the people, from his shoulder and upward (supra 9:2), and when Saul noticed this, he cast an envious glance toward him, and David realized it.

rashi.heb:
*ויואל ללכת.* 
תרגם יונתן: ולא אבה למיזל. יש תיבות משמשות לשון וחילופו, כמו (ישעיהו י לג): מסעף פארה ; (תהלים נב ז): ושרשך מארץ חיים:
rashi.eng: *ויאל ללכת.* and he did not want to go (in them - Jonathan.) (Despite the fact that ויאל usually means, he wanted, [cf., Ex. 2:21],) there are words which have two opposite definitions, e.g., “will cut off a branch (Is. 10:32),” (using מסעף, will cut off, derived from סעיף, a branch). And he will uproot you from the land of the living (Ps 52:7), (using ושרשך, will uproot you, derived from שרש, a root).

rashi.heb:
*כי לא נסה.* 
(תרגום:) ארי לא אליף:
rashi.eng: *for he was not accustomed.*  for he was not accustomed (after Jonathan)

rashi.heb:
*כי לא נסיתי.* 
(תרגום:) ארי לית בהון ניסא, אין שבחו של נס בכך. לשון אחר: ויואל ללכת, רצה ללכת ולנסות, וכאשר ראה שהיו כבדים עליו, הסירם:
rashi.eng: *for I am not accustomed.* (Heb. לא נסיתי (Jonathan explains this as derived from נס, a miracle, and, therefore, renders:) for there is no miracle in them, i.e., there will be no praise for the miracle in this manner. Another explanation is ויאל ללכת - he wanted to go, and to try, when he saw that they were too heavy for him, he took them off.

notes.520: (tn): This Hebrew word occurs only here and its exact meaning is not entirely clear. It refers to a receptacle of some sort and apparently was a common part of a shepherd’s equipment. Here it serves as a depository for the stones that David will use in his sling.

rashi.heb:
*חלוקי אבנים.* 
אבנים דקות וחלקות:
rashi.eng: *five smooth pebbles.* five thin, smooth stones.

rashi.heb:
*ובילקוט.* 
ובתרמיליה (תרגום:):
rashi.eng: *and in the sack.* (Jonathan renders:) ובתרמיליה.

notes.522: (sn): Sticks is a pejorative reference to David’s staff (v. 40); the same Hebrew word (מַקֵּל, maqqel) is used for both.

notes.523: (tc): Many medieval Hebrew mss have “the earth” here, instead of the MT’s “the field.”

rashi.heb:
*ולבהמת השדה.* 
אין דרך לבהמות לאכול אדם, אמר דוד: כבר נטרפה דעתו של זה, שלי הוא, בא דוד ואמר לו: ונתתי פגר מחנה פלשתים וגו' ולחית הארץ:
rashi.eng: *and to the cattle of the field.* It is not customary for cattle to eat human (sic) flesh. Said David “This one’s mind is already deranged (like one who is close to death). He is mine.” David then came and said “… and I shall give the carcasses of the camp of the Philistines… and to the beasts of the earth (not to the cattle).”

notes.524: (tc): Most LXX mss lack the second half of v. 48.

rashi.heb:
*ויפל על פניו.* 
לא היה לו לפול אלא לאחוריו, שהרי על מצחו הוכה, אלא כדי שלא יצטער דוד לילך ולחתוך את ראשו, שנשתכר דוד עכשיו שתים עשרה אמות וזרתים, שקומתו שש אמות וזרת, נשתכר מלא קומה לאחוריו, ומלא קומה לפניו (במדרש תהלים):
rashi.eng: *and he fell on his face to the ground.* He should have fallen backwards since he had been struck in the forehead. But, (he fell forward) in order that David should not be troubled to walk and sever his head, for David saved twelve cubits and two spans. Since his height was six cubits and a span, David saved (a walk of) his entire height back and his entire height forth.

notes.526: (tn): Verse 50 is a summary statement; v. 51 gives a more detailed account of how David killed the Philistine.

notes.527: (tn, Heb): “his”; the referent (Goliath) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.528: (tc): Most LXX mss lack the words “drew it from its sheath.”

notes.530: (tc): Most of the LXX ms tradition has here “Gath.”

rashi.heb:
*מדלוק.* 
מרדוף, כמו (בראשית לא לו): דלקת אחרי:
rashi.eng: *from pursuing.* (מדלק) Same as מרדף, similar to “you have pursued me” (דלקת) (Gen. 31: 36).

notes.531: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
notes.532: (tn, Heb): “his”; the referent (Goliath) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*בן מי זה הנער.* 
וכי לא היה מכירו, והלא כתיב (לעיל טז כא): ויאהבהו מאד ויהי לו נושא כליו, אלא ראהו מתנהג בטכסיסי מלכות, אמר שאול: אם בא ממשפחת פרץ, מלך יהיה, שהמלך פורץ גדר לעשות לו דרך ואין ממחין בידו, ואם ממשפחת זרח בא, חשוב יהיה. אמר לו דואג: עד שאתה שואל אם בא ממשפחה שיהא הוא הגון למלכות אם לאו, שאל אם ראוי לבא בקהל אם לאו, שהרי מרות המואביה בא. אמר לו אבנר: שנינו עמוני ולא עמונית. אמר לו דואג: אם כן ממזר ולא ממזרת. אמר לו: כאן נאמר (דברים כג ה): על דבר אשר לא קדמו אתכם בלחם ובמים, ואין דרך אשה בכך. אמר לו: היה להם לקדם אנשים לקראת אנשים, ונשים לקראת נשים. נשתתק אבנר, אמר לו שאול:
rashi.eng: *Whose son is this youth,.* Our Rabbis said: Did he not recognize him? Is it not stated: “And he became his weapon bearer” (supra 16:21)? But, (rather this is the explanation): he saw him behaving in a kingly manner. (Vid. supra v. 38) Said Saul, “If he comes from the family of Perez, he will be a king, for the king may break fences (פורץ, related to פרץ) to make a way for himself, and no one may stop him. If, however, he comes from the family of Zerah, he will merely become an esteemed person. Said Doeg to him, ” Before you ask whether or not he is descended from a family which qualifies him for the throne, ask whether or not he is qualified to enter the congregation, (i.e., whether or not he may marry among Jews) since he is descended from Ruth the Moabitess.“ Said Abner to him, ” We have learned: An Ammonite (is forbidden, Deut. 23:3) but not an Ammonitess. (Similarly, a Moabite is forbidden, but not a Moabitess.) “ Said Doeg to him, ” If so (let us say), a ‘mamzer’ (the male issue of a union forbidden under penalty of extinction is forbidden,) and not a ‘mamzereth’ (the female issue of such a union).“ He replied, ” It is stated here: Because they did not meet you with bread and water (v. 5 ibid.), and it is not customary for a woman to do so.“ He said to him,” Men should have met men, and women should have met women." Abner became silent. Saul said to him:

rashi.heb:
*שאל אתה בן מי זה העלם.* 
למעלה כתיב 'הנער', וכאן כתוב 'העלם', אמר לו: הלכה זו נתעלמה ממך, צא ושאל בבית המדרש, כדאיתא ביבמות (עו ב):
rashi.eng: *You ask whose son this youth is.* Above (v. 55) it is written: הנער, and here it is written העלם. He said to him, “This law has escaped your memory (נתעלמה). Go out and ask in the academy.” This is as it is stated in Jeb. 77a.

notes.534: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map7-E2; Map8-E2; Map10-B4.

notes.536: (tn, Heb): “the soul of Jonathan was bound with the soul of David.”
notes.537: (tn, Heb): “like his [own] soul.” On the nature of Jonathan’s love for David, see J. A. Thompson, “The Significance of the Verb Love in the David-Jonathan Narratives in 1 Samuel,” VT 24 (1974): 334-38.

notes.538: (tn, Heb): “him”; the referent (David) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

notes.540: (tn, Heb): “it was good in the eyes of all the people and also in the eyes of the servants of Saul.”

notes.541: (tn, Heb): “them.” The masculine plural pronoun apparently refers to the returning soldiers.
notes.542: (tn, Heb): “with tambourines, with joy, and with three-stringed instruments.”

rashi.heb:
*ובשלשים.* 
תרגם יונתן: ובצלצלין. מין כלי זמר:
rashi.eng: *and with cymbals.* (ובשלשים) - Jonathan renders: and with cymbals, a type of musical instrument.

rashi.heb:
*ועוד לו.* 
ועוד לו מה הוא נחסר שצריך להוסיף לו:
rashi.eng: *“… And what more can he have…”.* (lit., and he has yet; i.e.,) What more is he lacking, that he needs to acquire…

rashi.heb:
*אך המלוכה.* 
אינו צריך עוד אלא למלכות:
rashi.eng: *but the kingdom?.* He needs nothing else but the kingdom.

rashi.heb:
*עוין.* 
(תרגום:) עין רעה:
rashi.eng: *eyed.* with an envious glance.

notes.544: (tn): The Hebrew text adds here “with his hand.”

rashi.heb:
*יתנבא.* 
ואשתטי נביא ושוטה מדברים דברי רמזים שאינם ניכרים:
rashi.eng: *and he raved.* (lit., he prophesied. Jonathan renders:) and he raved. A prophet and a mad man speak with unintelligible hints.

rashi.heb:
*אכה בדוד ובקיר.* 
מכה אחת אכה, שיכנס החנית בדוד ובקיר:
rashi.eng: *“I shall pin David to the wall,”.* (lit., I shall strike David and the wall) I shall strike one blow that the spear will pierce David and the wall.

notes.545: (tn, Heb): “him”; the referent (David) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.547: (tn, Heb): “and he went out and came in before the people.” See v. 16.

rashi.heb:
*משכיל.* 
מצליח:

notes.549: (tc): Much of the ms evidence for the LXX lacks vv. 17-19.

rashi.heb:
*ושאול אמר.* 
בלבו:
rashi.eng: *and Saul said.* to himself (lit., in his heart).

rashi.heb:
*אל תהי ידי בו.* 
פן אענש:
rashi.eng: *Let not my hand be upon him.* lest I be punished.

rashi.heb:
*ותהי בו יד פלשתים.* 
לכך אמר לו והלחם מלחמות ה':
rashi.eng: *but let the hand of the Philistines be upon him..* Therefore, he said to him, ‘…and wage the wars of the Lord.’

notes.551: (tn, Heb): “Who are my relatives, the clan of my father?” The term חַי (khay), traditionally understood as “my life,” is here a rare word meaning “family, kinfolk” (see HALOT 309 s.v. III חַי). The phrase “clan of my father” may be a scribal gloss explaining the referent of this rare word.

rashi.heb:
*בעת תת.* 
כשהגיע זמן שקבעו לתתה לו, ובעוד שהיו מתעסקים לתתה לו, נתגלגל הדבר ונתנה לעדריאל:
rashi.eng: *at the time that Merab, Saul’s daughter, should have been given.* When the time which they had set to give her to him arrived, and while they were occupied with giving her to him, the matter turned out that she was given to Adriel.

notes.553: (tc): The final sentence of v. 21 is absent in most LXX mss.

rashi.heb:
*בשתים תתחתן בי.* 
שתי בנות יש לי, באחת מהן תתחתן בי וכן תרגם יונתן: בחדא מתרין. כיוצא בו (שמואל-ב כד יב): שלש אנכי נוטל עליך. אחת משלש, כמו שמפורש שם: בחר לך אחת מהם:
rashi.eng: *With two, shall you become my son-in-law.* I have two daughters. Through one of them, will you become my son-in-law. And so did Jonathan render: with one of two. Similar to this, (we find:) Three things I cast upon you (II Sam. 24:12), meaning, one of three things. As it is explained there, “Choose for yourself one of them.”

notes.556: (tn, Heb): “and it was acceptable in the eyes of David.”

rashi.heb:
*ולא מלאו הימים.* 
לא המתין עד מלאת הימים שקבע לו להביא את מאה הערלות:
rashi.eng: *and the days had not expired.* He did not wait until the expiration of the days which he had set for him to bring the hundred foreskins.

rashi.heb:
*ויקם דוד וילך הוא ואנשיו וגו' וימלאום.* 
פרישנטי"ר בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *and they delivered them in full.* Presenter in French (to present).

notes.560: (tn, Heb): “Saul’s.” In the translation the proper name has been replaced by the pronoun for stylistic reasons.
notes.561: (tn, Heb): “him”; the referent (David) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

notes.562: (tn, Heb): “of David.” In the translation the proper name has been replaced by the pronoun for stylistic reasons.
notes.563: (tc, Heb): The final sentence of v. 29 is absent in most LXX mss. “all the days.”

rashi.heb:
*לרא.* 
ליראה:
rashi.eng: *afraid.* (לרא), equivalent to ליראה (to fear).

notes.564: (tc): Verse 30 is absent in most LXX mss.

rashi.heb:
*ויצאו שרי פלשתים.* 
לבא בגדודים לשלול שלל בישראל:
rashi.eng: *And the princes of the Philistines came out.* to come in troops to plunder the Israelites.

rashi.heb:
*ליד אבי.* 
סמוך לאבי, איינשיי"ש בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *beside my father.* (lit., at the hand of my father.) Near my father, ‘en son aise’ (‘on his side,’ from Latin ‘adiacentia,’ adjacent) in Old French.

notes.570: (tn, Heb): “spoke good with respect to David.”

notes.572: (tn, Heb): “and he put his life into his hand.”

notes.573: (tn, Heb): “and Saul listened to the voice of Jonathan.”

notes.574: (tn, Heb): “and he was before him as before.”

notes.575: (tn, Heb): “and he struck them down with a great blow.”

notes.577: (tn): The Hebrew text adds here “with his hand.”

notes.578: (tn, Heb): “and he drove the spear into the wall.”

notes.581: (tn, Heb): “teraphim” (also a second time in this verse and once in v. 16). These were statues that represented various deities. According to 2 Kgs 23:24 they were prohibited during the time of Josiah’s reform movement in the seventh century. The idol Michal placed under the covers was of sufficient size to give the mistaken impression that David lay in the bed, thus facilitating his escape.
notes.582: (tn): The exact meaning of the Hebrew word כָּבִיר (kavir) is uncertain; it is found in the Hebrew Bible only here and in v. 16. It probably refers to a quilt made of goat’s hair, perhaps used as a fly net while one slept. See HALOT 458 s.v. *כָּבִיר. Cf. KJV, TEV “pillow”; NLT “cushion”; NAB, NRSV “net.”
notes.583: (tn, Heb): “at the place of its head.”

rashi.heb:
*ותקח מיכל.* 
כדי שלא יבינו שברח וירדפו אחריו:
rashi.eng: *she put… at its head.* since the teraphim has no hair, and this resembles human hair.

rashi.heb:
*את התרפים.* 
עשויים בדמות גוף אדם:
rashi.eng: *And Michal took.* so that they should not understand that he fled, and pursue him.

rashi.heb:
*כביר העזים.* 
עור מופשט שלם כחמת, פלוצי"ל בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *the teraphim.* made in the likeness of a human body.

rashi.heb:
*שמה מראשותיו.* 
לפי שאין לתרפים שיער, וזה דומה לשיער אדם:
rashi.eng: *a goatskin.* A hide skinned in one piece, like a skin bottle. Flocete in French (a hairy stuff).

notes.584: (tn, Heb): “Send me away! Why should I kill you?” The question has the force of a threat in this context. See P. K. McCarter, I Samuel (AB), 325, 26.

rashi.heb:
*הוא אמר אלי וגו'.* 
אתה מסרתני ביד לסטים אחד, שלף חרבו עלי עד ששלחתיו:
rashi.eng: *He said to me, ‘Let me go, etc.’.* You delivered me into the hands of a bandit. He drew his sword over me until I allowed him to leave.

rashi.heb:
*בניות.* 
(תרגום:) בבית אולפנא:
rashi.eng: *and stayed in Naioth.* (lit., dwellings; Jonathan renders:) in the house of study.

rashi.heb:
*להקת.* 
(תרגום:) סיעת:
rashi.eng: *the company.* להקת, reversed from קהלת a company (Jonathan).

notes.585: (tn, Heb): “he” (also in v. 23). the referent (Saul) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*ויפשט גם הוא בגדיו.* 
בגדי מלכות, ללבוש בגדי התלמידים:
rashi.eng: *And he too stripped off his clothes.* his royal garments, to don the garments of the disciples.

rashi.heb:
*ויפול ערום.* 
ונפל ברשן, תרגם יונתן: ונפל ערטילאי. ובשם רבי מנחם ששמע מפי ערבי אחד: 'ברשן' בלשון ערבי משוגע:
rashi.eng: *And he fell naked.* (Rashi’s commentary, as it appears in available editions, is very difficult, and probably erroneous. I should like to take the liberty to emend the text to read:) And he fell naked. Jonathan renders: ונפל ברשן, and in the name of Rabbi Menahem, who heard from an Arab, ברשן in Arabic means insane.

notes.587: (tn, Heb): “and he came and said before Jonathan.”

notes.589: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Jonathan) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.590: (tc): The translation follows the Qere, many medieval Hebrew mss, and the ancient versions in reading “he will not do,” rather than the Kethib of the MT (“do to him”).

notes.592: (tc): The LXX and the Syriac Peshitta lack the word “again.”
notes.593: (tn): The infinitive absolute appears before the finite verb for emphasis.
notes.594: (tn, Heb): “said,” that is, to himself. So also in v. 25.

rashi.heb:
*כפשע.* 
כפסיעה אחת נפטרתי מפניו, והכה בחנית בקיר, באותה פסיעה נצלתי מן המות:
rashi.eng: *there is but a step between me and death.* With (or about) one step I drew away from before him, and he drove the spear into the wall. With that step, I was saved from death.

notes.595: (tn, Heb): “whatever your soul says, I will do for you.”

notes.596: (tn, Heb): “and I must surely sit with the king to eat.” The infinitive absolute appears before the finite verb for emphasis.

rashi.heb:
*הנה חדש מחר.* 
חידוש הלבנה, וכל אוכלי שולחן המלך אין נמנע איש מלבא ביום טוב אל הלחם:
rashi.eng: *Behold tomorrow is the new moon.* (Heb. ‘hodesh,’ from ‘hadash,’ new.) The renewal of the moon. And of all those who eat at the King’s table, no one refrains from coming to the repast on the festive day.

rashi.heb:
*ואנכי ישוב אשב עם המלך לאכול.* 
לשון הווה הוא, ואנכי רגיל לישב עם המלך תמיד לאכול סמוך לו:
rashi.eng: *and I am accustomed to eat with the king.* (ואנכי ישב אשב) This is the present tense meaning ‘and I am accustomed to sit with the king regularly to eat beside him.’

rashi.heb:
*ושלחתני.* 
מעתה, ונסתרתי עד הערב של יום שלישי, ולא אהיה עם האוכלים, ויפקד מושבי, ויתמה המלך עלי, או מחר או למחרתו:
rashi.eng: *And you shall let me go.* from now, and I shall hide until the evening of the third day, and I shall not be with the eaters and my seat will be vacant, and the king will wonder about me either tomorrow or the day after tomorrow.

notes.598: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map7-E2; Map8-E2; Map10-B4.

rashi.heb:
*נשאול נשאל.* 
רשות שאל ממני:
rashi.eng: *took leave.* (lit., asked) He asked me for permission.

rashi.heb:
*זבח הימים.* 
משנה לשנה בזמן הזה:
rashi.eng: *the yearly sacrifice.* from year to year at this time.

notes.600: (tn, Heb): “know that the evil is completed from with him.”

rashi.heb:
*אם כה יאמר טוב.* 
שלא יחרה לו:
rashi.eng: *If he says thus, ‘Good’.* i.e., he is not angry.

rashi.heb:
*שלום לעבדך.* 
אין בלבו להרגני:
rashi.eng: *then it is well with your bondsman.* He does not have in mind to kill me.

rashi.heb:
*ואם חרה יחרה.* 
זהו שאהא לו מצוי להרגני:
rashi.eng: *but if he becomes angry.* This is proof that he wants me to be accessible to him to kill me.

rashi.heb:
*כלתה הרעה מעמו.* 
סוף דבר מחשבה רעה לו עלי:
rashi.eng: *the evil has been decided upon by him.* (lit., the evil has been ended from him) - The end of the matter is, that he has an evil thought concerning me.

notes.602: (tn, Heb): “for into a covenant of the Lord you have brought your servant with you.”
notes.603: (tn, Heb): “and if there is in me guilt.”

rashi.heb:
*ועשית חסד.* 
לשלחני:
rashi.eng: *And you shall do kindness.* to let me go.

rashi.heb:
*חלילה לך.* 
כזאת לחשדני שאדע בו שכלתה מעמו הרעה ולא אגיד לך:
rashi.eng: *Far be it from you.* to suspect me thus, that I should know that evil has been decided upon by him, and not reveal it to you.

rashi.heb:
*מי יגיד לי.* 
במקום שאסתר שם:
rashi.eng: *Who will tell me.* in the place where I shall be hidden?

notes.604: (tc): The Hebrew text has simply “the Lord God of Israel.” On the basis of the Syriac version, many reconstruct the text to read “[is] my witness,” which may have fallen out of the text by homoioarcton (an error which is entirely possible if עֵד, ’ed, “witness,” immediately followed ַָדוִד, “David,” in the original text).

rashi.heb:
*ה' אלהי ישראל.* 
לשון שבועה:
rashi.eng: *(By) the Lord God of Israel.* This is an expression of an oath.

rashi.heb:
*השלשית.* 
בימי מחר, זהו יום שלישי כשעה של עכשיו, כי מחר חדש, ושמא לא יתמה מחר אבי, אבל יתמה ביום השלישי:
rashi.eng: *the third morrow.* of the following day. That means the third day at this time, for tomorrow is the new moon, and perhaps my father will not wonder (about your absence) tomorrow, but will wonder on the third day.

rashi.heb:
*כה יעשה לי.* 
הקב"ה,
rashi.eng: *So shall do to me.* the Holy One, Blessed be He. (This is an obvious error, and should read:)

rashi.heb:
*כי אחקור את אבי.* 
ואמצא שהוא טוב אליך, אם לא אשלח על ידי שליח וגליתי אזנך, כי הטובה אני יכול לגלות, ואם ייטיב אל אבי להרע לך, אותה לא אגלה, פן יודע לאבי מקום שאתה שם, וגליתי אני בעצמי את אזנך:
rashi.eng: *So shall the Lord do to Jonathan..* When I sound out my father and find that he is favorable toward you if I do not send by way of messenger and reveal to you, for good I am able to reveal. And if it pleases my father to do evil to you, that I shall not reveal (by messenger), lest your whereabouts become known to my father, but I myself, shall reveal it to you.

rashi.heb:
*ולא אם עודני חי.* 
לשון בקשה הוא, כמו (מלכים-ב ה יז): ולא יתן נא לעבדיך. ואינו זז ממשמעו, ולא תעשה לי טובה בעודני חי, שתעשה עמי חסד ה' בטרם אמות, ומהו החסד, שלא תכרית את חסדך מעם ביתי, בזאת תכרות לי ברית בחיי:
rashi.eng: *And please, if I am still alive..* (ולא אם עודני חי) An expression of request, like ולא and if only it will be given to your bondsman (II Kings 5:17). It is, however, not removed from its usual sense, i.e., “and will you not do with me the kindness of the Lord before I die?” And what is the kindness? That you will not discontinue your kindness with my household. Regarding this, you shall make a covenant with me in my lifetime.

rashi.heb:
*ולא בהכרית ה'.* 
וגם לא תסיר חסדך מה', כי אף בבא הפורענות על בית אבי, שידעתי שיכרית המקום את אויביך:
rashi.eng: *and not even when the Lord cuts off.* And also, you shall not remove your kindness from them (מהם) even when retribution befalls my father’s house, for I know that the Lord will cut off your enemies.

notes.608: (tn, Heb): “cut.” The object of the verb (“covenant”) must be supplied.
notes.609: (tn): The word order is different in the Hebrew text, which reads “and Jonathan cut with the house of David, and the Lord will seek from the hand of the enemies of David.” The translation assumes that the main clauses of the verse have been accidentally transposed in the course of transmission. The first part of the verse (as it stands in MT) belongs with v. 17, while the second part of the verse actually continues v. 15.

rashi.heb:
*ובקש ה'.* 
את הברית הזאת:
rashi.eng: *and the Lord demanded it.* this covenant.

rashi.heb:
*מיד אויבי דוד.* 
כנה הכתוב, ופירושו: בקש הקב"ה את העון מיד דוד, כשעבר על הברית ואמר למפיבושת (שמואל-ב יט ל): אתה וציבא תחלקו את השדה, יצתה בת קול ואמרה: רחבעם וירבעם יחלקו את המלכות (שבת נו ב). וכן תרגם יונתן: ואתפרע ליה ה' מיד שנאי דוד:
rashi.eng: *from the hand of David’s enemies.* The Scripture euphemized. Its real meaning is: The Holy One, Blessed be He, demanded the punishment of the transgression from David’s hand. When he transgressed the covenant, and said to Mephibosheth, “You and Ziba shall divide the field” (II Sam. 19:30), a bath-kol came forth, and said, “Rehoboam and Jeroboam shall divide the kingdom.” And so did Jonathan render: and the Lord took retribution from David’s enemies.

notes.610: (tn, Heb): “for [with] the love of his [own] life he loved him.”

rashi.heb:
*מחר חדש.* 
ודרך כל אוכלי שולחן המלך לבא ביום מועד אל השולחן:
rashi.eng: *Tomorrow is the new moon.* and it is the custom of all those who eat at the king’s table to come on the festive day to the table.

rashi.heb:
*ונפקדת.* 
אבי יפקדך וישאל היכן אתה:
rashi.eng: *and you will be remembered.* My father will remember you, and ask where you are.

rashi.heb:
*כי יפקד מושבך.* 
שיהיה מושבך חסר, שאתה יושב בו וכן תרגם יונתן: ותתבעי ארי יהי מרוח בית אסחרותך:
rashi.eng: *for your seat will be vacant.* for your seat in which you sit, will be vacant, and so did Jonathan render: and you will be sought, for your seat will be vacant.

rashi.heb:
*ונפקדת.* 
לשון זכרון:
rashi.eng: *and you will be remembered.* [ונפקדת is] an expression of remembering.

rashi.heb:
*כי יפקד.* 
לשון חסרון:
rashi.eng: *will be vacant.* [יפקד is] an expression of lacking.

notes.611: (tc, Heb): “you will do [something] a third time.” The translation assumes an emendation of the verb from שִׁלַּשְׁתָּ (shillashta, “to do a third time”) to שִׁלִּישִׁית (shillishit, “[on the] third [day]”).
notes.612: (tn, Heb): “you must go down greatly.” See Judg 19:11 for the same idiom.
notes.613: (tn, Heb): “on the day of the deed.” This probably refers to the incident recorded in 19:2.

rashi.heb:
*ושלשת.* 
שלשת ימים, ואז תרד מאוד, כלומר לכשתגיע היום השלישי, תרד במקום סתר ותתחבא הרבה, כי אז יבקשוך, ובאת אל המקום הסתר הזה אשר אתה נסתר בו היום, שהוא יום מעשה מלאכה וכן תרגם יונתן: ביומא דחולא, שאותו היום נסתר, כמה שנאמר (פסוק כד): 'ויסתר דוד בשדה' מיד, 'ויהי החדש' מחר:
rashi.eng: *And for three days you shall hide very well.* And you shall triple the days, and then you shall descend very much, i.e., when the third day arrives, you shall descend into a secret place, and hide very well, for then they will seek you. And you shall come to this secret place, wherein you are hiding today, which is a workday. And so did Jonathan render: on the weekday, for he hid on that day, as it is stated: (infra v. 24) “And David hid in the field;” immediately, “and it was the new moon” on the morrow.

rashi.heb:
*האבן האזל.* 
אבן שהיתה אות להולכי דרכים:
rashi.eng: *the travelers’ stone.* (Heb. ‘even-ha azel,’ lit., the going stone, i.e.) a stone which was a sign (a landmark) for travelers.

rashi.heb:
*האזל.* 
הולכי הדרך, וכן תרגם יונתן: אבן אתא, אבן האות:
rashi.eng: *Ha-azel.* those who go on the road. And so did Jonathan render: even atha, the stone which was a sign.

rashi.heb:
*צדה אורה.* 
לא מפיק ה"א, ופתרון צדה כמו לצד, כל תיבה שצריכה למ"ד בתחלתה, הטיל לה ה"א בסופה, בצד אותה אבן, אורה חצים למטרה, כדי שלא יבין הנער, וזה סימן יהיה לך לנחש אם אתה צריך לברוח:
rashi.eng: *to the side, I shall shoot.* This is not a ‘mappiq-heh’ (aspirate ‘heh’). צדה is to be interpreted like לצד, to a side, for every word which requires a ‘lamed’ as a prefix, the Scripture gives a ‘he’ as a suffix. (Jeb. 13b) At the side of that stone, I shall shoot arrows to a mark, so that the youth will not understand, and this sign shall be for you to divine whether you must flee.

rashi.heb:
*והנה אשלח וגו'.* 
ודרך המבקש חץ הירוי, הולך עד מקום שרואה שהחץ הולך, ואינו יכול לכוין יפה, פעמים שהוא מחפשה והחץ להלן ממנו, ופעמים שהוא הולך להלן מן החץ ומחפשה, והניחוש הזה יהיה לך:
rashi.eng: *And behold, I shall send, etc..* And it is customary for one who seeks an arrow which has been shot, to go to the place where he sees the arrow flying, but he cannot ascertain exactly. Sometimes he searches for it, and the arrow is beyond him, and sometimes he goes beyond the arrow and searches for it, and you shall have this sign.

rashi.heb:
*אם אמור אומר לנער וגו' קחנו ובואה.* 
צא אתה בעצמך ממקום מחבואך, וקחנו ובוא אלי, כי אין לך לירא, כי שלום לך, הקב"ה חפץ שתהא כאן ולא תירא, ואפילו שמעתי מאבא רעה:
rashi.eng: *If I say to the youth… take it and come.* you yourself emerge from your hiding place, and take it, and come to me, for you have not to fear, for it is well with you. The Holy One Blessed be He, desires that you be here, and even if I have heard evil from Father.

rashi.heb:
*ואם כה אומר וגו' לך כי שלחך.* 
הקב"ה אומר לך לברוח ולהמלט:
rashi.eng: *But, if I say thus… Go! For the Lord has sent you away.* The Holy One Blessed be He tells you to flee and escape.

notes.616: (tc, Heb): “the Lord [is] between me and between you forever.” The translation assumes that the original text read עֵד עַד־עוֹלָם (’ed ’ad-’olam), “a witness forever,” with the noun “a witness” accidentally falling out of the text by haplography. See P. K. McCarter, I Samuel (AB), 338.

rashi.heb:
*והדבר אשר דברנו.* 
ברית שכרתנו יחד:
rashi.eng: *And concerning the matter which we have spoken.* the covenant which we made together.

rashi.heb:
*הנה ה' ביני וביניך.* 
עד על אותו דבר:
rashi.eng: *behold, the Lord is between me and you.* as Witness concerning that matter.

notes.617: (tc, Heb): “and Jonathan arose.” Instead of MT’s וַיָּקָם (vayyaqam, “and he arose”; from the hollow verbal root קוּם, qum), the translation assumes a reading וַיִּקַדֵּם (vayyiqaddem, “and he was in front of”; from the verbal root קדם, qdm). See P. K. McCarter, I Samuel (AB), 338.
notes.618: (tn, Heb): “and Abner sat at the side of Saul.”

rashi.heb:
*אל מושב הקיר.* 
בראש המטה אצל הקיר:
rashi.eng: *the seat by the wall.* at the head of the couch beside the wall.

rashi.heb:
*ויקם יהונתן.* 
עמד ממקומו, לפי שאין דרך הבן להיות מיסב אצל אביו, שדרכן היה לאכול מסובין על המטות, והיה דוד מיסב בין יהונתן ובין שאול, עכשיו שלא בא דוד, לא היסב יהונתן, עד שישב אבנר מצד שאול, ואחר כך ישב יהונתן מצד אבנר ואם תאמר לא ישב כלל, הרי הוא אומר (פסוק לד): ויקם יהונתן מעל השלחן, מכלל שישב:
rashi.eng: *and Jonathan arose.* He got up from his place, since it is not proper for a son to recline beside his father. Since their custom was to eat reclining on couches and David would recline between Jonathan and Saul, now that David did not come, Jonathan did not recline until Abner sat down beside Saul, and afterwards, Jonathan sat beside Abner. And if you say that he did not sit at all, the Scripture states: (infra v. 34) “And Jonathan arose from the table,” implying that he had been sitting.

notes.619: (tn): The words “about it” are not present in the Hebrew text, although they are implied.

rashi.heb:
*מקרה הוא.* 
קרי ראה:
rashi.eng: *It is an incident.* He has experienced a seminal emission.

rashi.heb:
*בלתי טהור הוא.* 
ועדיין לא טבל לקריו, שאלו טבל לקריו, אין צריך הערב שמש לחולין:
rashi.eng: *he is not clean.* and he has not yet immersed himself, for had he immersed himself for the uncleanness of his emission, he would not have to wait until sunset in order to eat ordinary food.

rashi.heb:
*כי לא טהור.* 
זו היא נתינת טעם לדבר, לפי שאינו טהור, לפיכך לא בא, שלא יטמא את הסעודה:
rashi.eng: *for he is not clean.* This clause gives the reason for the matter; i.e., since he is not clean, he, therefore, did not come, lest he contaminate the feast.

rashi.heb:
*ממחרת החדש.* 
ממחרת חידוש הלבנה:
rashi.eng: *on the morrow of the new moon.* on the morrow of the renewal of the moon.

rashi.heb:
*השני.* 
ביום שני לחדש:
rashi.eng: *the second.* on the second day of the month.

rashi.heb:
*והוא צוה לי אחי.* 
גדול הבית צוה לי שאהיה שם, והוא אחי אליאב:
rashi.eng: *and he, my brother, commanded me.* The eldest of the house, commanded me that I be there. And he is my brother Eliab.

rashi.heb:
*אמלטה.* 
אשקמוצי"ד בלע"ז, אלך יום אחד ואבוא:
rashi.eng: *let me slip away.* ‘Escamoter’ in French. I shall go away for one day and come back.

notes.624: (tc): Many medieval Hebrew mss include the words “his son” here.
notes.625: (tn, Heb): “son of a perverse woman of rebelliousness.” But such an overly literal and domesticated translation of the Hebrew expression fails to capture the force of Saul’s unrestrained reaction. Saul, now incensed and enraged over Jonathan’s liaison with David, is actually hurling very coarse and emotionally charged words at his son. The translation of this phrase suggested by Koehler and Baumgartner is “bastard of a wayward woman” (HALOT 796 s.v. עוה), but this is not an expression commonly used in English. A better English approximation of the sentiments expressed here by the Hebrew phrase would be “You stupid son of a bitch!” However, sensitivity to the various public formats in which the Bible is read aloud has led to a less startling English rendering which focuses on the semantic value of Saul’s utterance (i.e., the behavior of his own son Jonathan, which he viewed as both a personal and a political betrayal [= “traitor”]). But this concession should not obscure the fact that Saul is full of bitterness and frustration. That he would address his son Jonathan with such language, not to mention his apparent readiness even to kill his own son over this friendship with David (v. 33), indicates something of the extreme depth of Saul’s jealousy and hatred of David.

rashi.heb:
*נעות המרדות.* 
לשון נע, אשה נעה ונדה, יוצאנית, כאשר תאמר 'זעוה' מן 'זע', כן תאמר 'נעוה' מן 'נע', והתי"ו מן הדיבוק, שהוא דבוק למרדות:
rashi.eng: *a straying woman, deserving of punishment.* (בן נעות המרדות) An expression of straying and wandering, נע ונד, a gadding woman. Just as you say זעוה from זע, and the ‘tav’ is for the construct state, for it is connected to the word המרדות.

rashi.heb:
*המרדות.* 
שהיא ראויה לרדות ולייסר דבר אחר: כשחטפו בני בנימן מבנות שילה שיצאו לחול בכרמים, היה שאול ביישן ולא רצה לחטוף, עד שבאתה היא עצמה והעיזה פניה ורדפה אחריו:
rashi.eng: *deserving of punishment.* (Heb. המרדות), who deserves to be chastised and disciplined. Another explanation is as follows: When the men of Benjamin grabbed the girls of Shiloh, who came out to dance in the vineyards (Jud. 21:21), Saul was bashful, and did not want to grab [a girl], until she came herself, behaving insolently, and pursued him.

rashi.heb:
*נעות.* 
על שם הכרמים, והיא גת, כמו (עבודה זרה עד ב): נעוה ארתחו. יטופון נעווהי בחמר (תרגום פרשת ויחי פסוק חכלילי עינים (בראשית מט יב)), ולא מן השם:
rashi.eng: *straying woman.*  because of the vineyards. And that is a winepress, like (the Talmudical passage): Purge the winepress (which was used for forbidden wine) (Ab. Zarah 74b); His winepresses will drip with wine (Targum Onkelos, Gen. 40:12)….(The last three words of Rashi are incomprehensible, and are probably erroneous. The correct version is unknown to us.)

notes.627: (tn): The words “some men” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.

notes.629: (tn, Heb): “him”; the referent (Jonathan) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

notes.631: (tn, Heb): “for he was upset concerning David for his father had humiliated him.” The referent of the pronoun “him” is not entirely clear, but the phrase “concerning David” suggests that it refers to David, rather than Jonathan.

rashi.heb:
*נעצב אל דוד.* 
בשביל דוד:
rashi.eng: *he was grieved (lit.) to David.* concerning David.

rashi.heb:
*כי הכלימו אביו.* 
בשביל דוד:
rashi.eng: *for his father had put him to shame.* concerning David.

rashi.heb:
*למועד דוד.* 
למועד אשר קבע לו דוד:
rashi.eng: *at David’s appointed time.* at the time which David had set for him.

notes.632: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Jonathan) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*להעבירו.* 
החצי עבר את הנער:
rashi.eng: *to cause it to go beyond him..* The arrow went beyond the boy.

notes.635: (tc): The translation follows the LXX in reading “the mound,” rather than the MT’s “the south.” It is hard to see what meaning the MT reading “from beside the south” would have as it stands, since such a location lacks specificity. The NIV treats it as an elliptical expression, rendering the phrase as “from the south side of the stone (rock NCV).” This is perhaps possible, but it seems better to follow the LXX rather than the MT here.

rashi.heb:
*מאצל הנגב.* 
(תרגום:) מסטר אבן אתא דלקבל דרומא:
rashi.eng: *from a place toward the south.* (lit., from by the south. Jonathan renders:) from the side of the travelers’ (or sign) stone which was toward the south.

rashi.heb:
*עד דוד הגדיל.* 
הרבה לבכות:
rashi.eng: *until David exceeded.* He cried more.

notes.637: : sn Beginning with 20:42b, the verse numbers through 21:15 in the English Bible differ from the verse numbers in the Hebrew text (BHS), with 20:42b ET = 21:1 HT, 21:1 ET = 21:2 HT, 21:2 ET = 21:3 HT, etc., through 21:15 ET = 21:16 HT. With 22:1 the verse numbers in the ET and HT are again the same.
notes.638: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (David) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*לך לשלום.* 
והשבועה אשר נשבענו, ה' יהיה עד עליה עד עולם:
rashi.eng: *Go in peace!.* And the oath which we have sworn, may the Lord be witness thereon forever.

notes.640: (tn, Heb): “let not a man know anything about the matter [for] which I am sending you and [about] which I commanded you.”
notes.642: (tn): The Hebrew expression here refers to a particular, but unnamed, place. It occurs in the OT only here, in 2 Kgs 6:8, and in Ruth 4:1, where Boaz uses it to refer to Naomi’s unnamed kinsman-redeemer. A contracted form of the expression appears in Dan 8:13.

rashi.heb:
*ואת הנערים יודעתי.* 
לשון טורח, הנערים אשר יצאו עמי, הטרחתים לרוץ לפני אל מקום פלוני אלמוני:
rashi.eng: *And I troubled the young men.* (Heb. ‘va’yada’) An expression of troubling. The young men who came out with me, I have troubled them to run before me to a hidden, secret place.

rashi.heb:
*יודעתי.* 
כמו (שופטים ח טז): ויודע בהם את אנשי סכות:
rashi.eng: *I troubled.* similar to, “And with them he broke (va’yoda) the men of Succoth” (Jud. 8:16).

rashi.heb:
*פלוני אלמוני.* 
'אלמון' מאין שם, שאיני חפץ להזכיר, כי דבר סתר הוא:
rashi.eng: *hidden, secret.* (Heb. ‘ploni almoni.’) ‘Almoni’ is derived from ‘almon’ (a widower), bereft of a name, (as a widower is bereft of his spouse), for I do not wish to mention it, since it is a secret matter.

rashi.heb:
*פלוני.* 
כמו (דברים יז ח): 'כי יפלא', יתכסה:
rashi.eng: *hidden.* (Heb. ‘ploni,’) like: ‘ki yipalei’ (Deut. 17:8), which means ‘will be concealed.’

notes.645: (tn, Heb): “have kept themselves from women” (so NASB, NIV, NRSV); TEV “haven’t had sexual relations recently”; NLT “have not slept with any women recently.”

rashi.heb:
*או הנמצא.* 
אם אין חמשה, תן לי מה שנמצא בידך:
rashi.eng: *or whatever is found..* If there are not five, give me whatever is found in your possession.

rashi.heb:
*אך מאשה.* 
בקושי אני מאכילן לזרים, אך זה אי אפשר שאכילנו לטמאים:
rashi.eng: *but… from women.* With difficulty, I give them to strangers (non-priests) to eat, but it is impossible to give it to unclean people.

rashi.heb:
*עצורה לנו.* 
עצורה ממנו:
rashi.eng: *withheld from us..* lit., withheld to us.

rashi.heb:
*ויהיו כלי הנערים קדש.* 
טהורים:
rashi.eng: *and the young men’s garments are hallowed.* i.e., ritually clean.

rashi.heb:
*והוא דרך חול.* 
והלחם משנסתלק מעל השולחן והקטירו הבזיכין, קרוב הוא להיות חולין, שיצא מידי מעילה משיהיה לו שעת היתר לכהנים:
rashi.eng: *and that is in a manner common.* and the bread, since it has been removed from the table, and they have burned the spoonfuls (of frankincense), it is almost common, since it has been excluded from the prohibition of ‘me’ilah’ (betrayal) from the time it is permitted for the priests.

rashi.heb:
*ואף כי היום יקדש בכלי.* 
ואפילו אם היום היתה תחלת קדושתו על השלחן, הייתי זקוק ליטלו משם ולהאכילנו, שאחזו בולמוס ומסוכן הוא, כך מפורש במנחות:
rashi.eng: *and even if today it would be hallowed in the vessel.* and even if today were the commencement of its sanctity on the table, I should (or perhaps it should read, ‘you would’) be obliged to take it from there and feed us, for a ravenous hunger has seized me, and my life is in danger. Thus it is explained in Men. (95b).

rashi.heb:
*לשום לחם חם.* 
אחר, ביום הלקח זה ורבותינו אמרו (יומא כא א): חם ביום הלקחו, גם ביום סלוקו, חם כיום סדורו:
rashi.eng: *to place warm bread.* i. e., other warm bread on the day this was taken away. And our Rabbis said: Warm on the day it was taken - It was as warm on the day it was taken as it was on the day it was arranged.

rashi.heb:
*נעצר לפני ה'.* 
עוצר עצמו לפני אהל מועד, לעסוק בתורה:
rashi.eng: *detained before the Lord.* he tarried before the tent of meeting to engage in Torah.

rashi.heb:
*אביר הרועים.* 
אב בית דין:
rashi.eng: *the chief of Saul’s shepherds.* the head of the tribunal.

rashi.heb:
*ואין יש פה.* 
ואם יש פה:
rashi.eng: *ואין יש פה.* And if there is here.

rashi.heb:
*נחוץ.* 
בבהילות:
rashi.eng: *urgent.* hurried.

rashi.heb:
*לוטה.* 
כרוכה, וכן (מלכים-א יט יג): וילט פניו באדרתו:
rashi.eng: *wrapped.* (Heb (לוטה wrapped, and so: “and be wrapped (וילט) his face in his mantle” (I Kings 19:13).

rashi.heb:
*אחרי האפוד.* 
אחר ששאלו באורים ותומים, אמר לו כן וכן תרגם יונתן: בתר דשאיל ליה באפודא:
rashi.eng: *behind the ephod.* (after the ephod) after he had consulted the Urim and Tummim for him. And so did Jonathan render: after he asked the ephod for him.

notes.647: (tn, Heb): “placed these matters in his heart.”

rashi.heb:
*הלא זה דוד מלך הארץ.* 
אמרו לו לאכיש, תנאי היה בינינו (לעיל יז ט): 'אם יוכל להלחם אתי והכני והיינו לכם לעבדים', אין לך אלא שתרד מכסאך, ויהיה מלך הארץ הזאת:
rashi.eng: *Is this not David the king of the land?.* They said to Achish, There was a stipulation between us, (supra 17:9) “If he is able to fight with me and kill me, we shall be slaves to you.” You have nothing to do but get off your throne and let him become king of this land.

rashi.heb:
*את טעמו.* 
את דבריו:
rashi.eng: *his speech.* his speech.

rashi.heb:
*ויתהולל.* 
נשתטה:
rashi.eng: *and he feigned insanity.* and he feigned insanity.

rashi.heb:
*ויתו.* 
ויכתוב:
rashi.eng: *and he scribbled.* he wrote.

rashi.heb:
*רירו.* 
רוקו, דבר הנוטף קרוי ריר, וכן (איוב ו ו): בריר חלמות ; וכן (ויקרא טו ג): רר בשרו:
rashi.eng: *his saliva.* (Heb. ‘riro’) his saliva. Anything which drips is called ‘rir,’ and so: “in saliva (b’rir) of health” (Job 6:7), and so: “whether his flesh run (rar)” (Lev. 15:3).

rashi.heb:
*הזה יבא אל ביתי.* 
לשון תמיהה, ולכך נקוד חטף פתח, ורפי:
rashi.eng: *Will this one come into my house?.* (הזה)This is a question form. It is therefore punctuated by a “hataf patah” (under the ‘heh’), and (the ‘zain’) is not punctuated by a ‘dagesh.’

rashi.heb:
*וישבו עמו כל ימי היות דוד במצודה.* 
סמוך למואב, וכשיצא דוד משם ליער חרת, הרג מלך מואב את אביו ואת אמו ואחיו, חוץ מאחד שבהם שהחייהו נחש העמוני, והוא החסד שאמר דוד (שמואל-ב יב): כאשר עשה אביו עמדי חסד, כדאיתא במדרש רבי תנחומא:
rashi.eng: *and they stayed with him all the time that David was in the stronghold.* near Moab, and when David went away from there to the forest of Heresh, the king of Moab slew his father, mother, and brothers, with the exception of one of them, whom Nahash the Ammonite preserved alive. And that is the kindness which David (meant when he) said, (II Sam. 10:2) “As his father did kindness with me,” as it is stated in the Mid. of Rabbi T. (T. Buber, Vayera 25).

notes.655: (tn, Heb): “and Saul heard that David and the men who were with him were known.”

rashi.heb:
*כי נודע דוד.* 
כי התבונן להשמר ממנו:
rashi.eng: *that David… had become known.* for he investigated, to beware of him.

rashi.heb:
*תחת האשל ברמה.* 
אחת שהיתה בגבול בנימן ורבותינו אמרו (תענית ה ב): היא היתה רמה של שמואל, ושני מקומות הן, וכן מדרשו: ושאול יושב בגבעה, בזכות האשל הגדול אשר ברמה, שהיה מתפלל עליו:
rashi.eng: *under the tamarisk tree on a hill.* (Heb. ‘b’ramah,’) on one hill, which was in the border of Benjamin. Our Rabbis, however, said: This was Samuel’s Ramah, and since these are two distinct places, it is expounded thus: Saul was sitting in Gibeah through the merit of the great tamarisk tree (Samuel) who was in Ramah, and was praying for him.

notes.656: (tc): The MT has “to all of you.” If this reading is correct, we have here an example of a prepositional phrase functioning as the equivalent of a dative of advantage, which is not impossible from a grammatical point of view. However, the LXX, the Syriac Peshitta, and Vulgate all have “and.” A conjunction rather than a preposition should probably be read on the front of this phrase.
notes.657: (tn, Heb): “officers of a thousand and officers of a hundred.”

rashi.heb:
*ושאול לו באלהים.* 
עשיתו מלך, שאין נשאלין באורים ותומים להדיוט:
rashi.eng: *and by inquiring of the Lord on his behalf.* You made him a king (by inquiring of the Urim and Tummim for him), since we may not inquire of the Urim and Tummim for a commoner.

rashi.heb:
*וסר אל משמעתך.* 
כמו (בראשית יט ג): ויסורו אליו, וקרב לשמושך ואל שמע דבריך, וכי היה לי להבין שאינו הולך בשליחותך:
rashi.eng: *and goes to do your service.* (וסר) like “And they turned to him (ויסורו)” (Gen. 19:6), meaning that he comes near to do your service and to do your commands. (The root סור, which usually means ‘to turn away,’ is used here to mean ‘to come near.’) Was I able to understand that he was not going on your mission?

rashi.heb:
*היום החלותי לשאל לו.* 
בתמיה, זה ימים רבים שצורך הצבור בו, שמינהו מוציא ומביא את ישראל, ומאז אני שואל לו באלהים:
rashi.eng: *Have I begun today to inquire.* This is a question, inferring as follows: It is already a long time that the community has need for him for he (i.e., the king) appointed him as the one who leads Israel to and from battle, and since then, I inquire of God on his behalf.

rashi.heb:
*חלילה לי.* 
מעשות דבר זה למרד ומעל:
rashi.eng: *Far be it from me.* to have done this thing with the intent of rebellion or treason.

notes.665: (tn, Heb): “to extend their hand to harm.”

rashi.heb:
*לרצים הנצבים עליו.* 
אבנר ועמשא היו:
rashi.eng: *who were standing beside him.* They were Abner and Amassa.

rashi.heb:
*ולא אבו.* 
דרשו אכין ורקין (יהושע א יח): כל איש אשר ימרה את פיך וגו', יכול אפילו לדבר עבירה תלמוד לומר 'רק':
rashi.eng: *And… would not.* They expounded ‘buts’ and ‘onlys.’ The Scripture states: “Every man who rebels against your command shall be put to death” (Jos. 1:18). One may think that this means even to commit a sin. The Scripture, therefore, states: Only (be strong and of good courage).

notes.666: (tc): The number is confused in the Greek ms tradition. The LXX, with the exception of the Lucianic recension, has the number 305. The Lucianic recension, along with a couple of Old Latin mss, has the number 350.

rashi.heb:
*לדויג.* 
נשתנה שמו, אמר לו נתפסת כדג, אתה הלשנת עליהם, אתה הרוג אותם:
rashi.eng: *to Doeg.* (the ‘kethib’ is דויג, upon which our Rabbis comment:) His name was changed (from דואג to דויג). He said to him, “You are caught like a fish. You informed on them. You slay them.”

notes.667: (tc): The translation follows the LXX, which reads “I am guilty,” rather than the MT, which has “I have turned.”

rashi.heb:
*אנכי סבתי.* 
סבבתי הדבר עד שבא לידי כך:
rashi.eng: *I brought about.* I brought about the matter until it came to this.

notes.668: (tn): Or “the one who.” This may refer specifically to Saul, in which case David acknowledges that Abiathar’s life is endangered because of his allegiance to David. The translation assumes that the statement is more generalized, meaning that any enemy of Abiathar is an enemy of David. In other words, David promises that he will protect Abiathar with his very own life.

rashi.heb:
*כי אשר יבקש את נפשי.* 
אדם אחד רודף שנינו, במקום שאמלט שם אני, תמלט אתה, כי במשמרתי תהיה תמיד, כך תרגם יונתן: ארי מאן דבעי למיקטלי בעי למקטלך. ויש עוד לפרש; כי אשר יאהבני יאהבך, ואשר ישמור את נפשי ישמור את נפשך, ויש דוגמא במקרא (משלי כט י): אנשי דמים ישנאו תם וישרים יבקשו נפשו, הרי כאן בקשת נפש לטובה:
rashi.eng: *for he who seeks my soul.* One man is pursuing both of us. Wherever I shall escape, you shall escape, for you will always be in my safeguard. Jonathan renders: for he who seeks to kill me, seeks to kill you. It may also be interpreted: for he who will love me, will love you, and he who will guard my soul, will guard your soul. There is another instance of this in the Scriptures: “Men of blood hate him that is sincere, but the upright seek his soul” (Prov. 29:10). Here is (an instance of) seeking a soul for good.

notes.669: (tn, Heb): “and struck them down with a great blow.”

notes.670: (tn, Heb): “an ephod went down in his hand.”

notes.671: (tn): The MT reading (“God has alienated him into my hand”) in v. 7 is a difficult and uncommon idiom. The use of this verb in Jer 19:4 is somewhat parallel, but not entirely so. Many scholars have therefore suspected a textual problem here, emending the word נִכַּר (nikkar, “alienated”) to סִכַּר (sikkar, “he has shut up [i.e., delivered]”). This is the idea reflected in the translations of the Syriac Peshitta and Vulgate, although it is not entirely clear whether they are reading something different from the MT or are simply paraphrasing what for them too may have been a difficult text. The LXX has “God has sold him into my hands,” apparently reading מַכַר (makar, “sold”) for MT’s נִכַּר. The present translation is a rather free interpretation.
notes.672: (tn, Heb): “with two gates and a bar.” Since in English “bar” could be understood as a saloon, it has been translated as an attributive: “two barred gates.”

rashi.heb:
*נכר אותו אלהים בידי.* 
הסגיר, וכן (עובדיה א יב): אל תרא ביום אחיך ביום נכרו. וממשקל החזקים הוא, כמו (איכה ב ט): אבד ושבר בריחיה. ואם בקש לדבר במשקולת הרפים, היה נקוד נכר:
rashi.eng: *God has delivered him into my hand.* (נכר) delivered, and so, “And do not look on, on the day of your brother, on the day of his being delivered” (Ob. 1:12). This is the conjugation of the strong verbs (piel, being punctuated by a dagesh in the middle letter of the root), like בריחיה אבד ושבר “He destroyed and broke her bars” (Lam. 21:9). (These words are punctuated in like manner.) If he desired to speak in the conjugation of the weak verbs, (Kal), it would have been punctuated thus: נכר.

rashi.heb:
*נסגר לבא בעיר דלתים ובריח.* 
ויבטח בכך, ולא יחוש לברוח ממנו:
rashi.eng: *for he has been shut in by coming into a city with doors and bars.* and he will rely on that, and will not take care to flee from me.

notes.673: (tn, Heb): “So Saul mustered all his army for battle to go down to Keilah to besiege against David and his men.”

notes.674: (tn, Heb): “Saul was planning the evil against him.”

rashi.heb:
*מחריש הרעה.* 
(תרגום:) כמין ית בישתא:
rashi.eng: *מחריש הרעה.* plotting the evil (from Jonathan).

rashi.heb:
*היסגרוני בעלי קעילה וגו'.* 
למדנו מכאן, שהשואל שני דברים, אין משיבין לו אלא אחד, ואין משיבין לו אלא ראשון, וכאן דוד שאל שלא כסדר, שהיה לו לשאול תחילה הירד שאול, היסגרוני בידו, והשיבוהו כסדר:
rashi.eng: *Will the citizens of Keilah deliver me.* We derive from here that one who inquires concerning two matters, receives a reply concerning one only, and he is only answered concerning the first one. And here, David asked in an inverted order, since he should have first asked, Will Saul come down? Will the citizens of Keilah deliver me? He was answered according to the order (in which he should have asked).

rashi.heb:
*באשר יתהלכו.* 
(תרגום:) באתר דכשר להלכא, במקום הצלתם:
rashi.eng: *wherever they would go.* (Jonathan renders:) in a place where it is proper to go, in a place where they would be saved.

notes.678: (tn, Heb): “him”; the referent (David) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*ויחזק את ידו.* 
חידש ברית שביניהם:
rashi.eng: *and he strengthened his hand.* He renewed the covenant which was between them.

notes.681: (tn, Heb): “to all the desire of your soul.”

rashi.heb:
*ולנו הסגירו.* 
ועלינו להסגירו:
rashi.eng: *ולא הסגירו.* and it is incumbent upon us to deliver him.

notes.682: (tn, Heb): “know and see.” The expression is a hendiadys. See also v. 23.
notes.683: (tn, Heb): “his place where his foot is.”

rashi.heb:
*כי אמר אלי.* 
מי שאמר:
rashi.eng: *For one told me.* (lit., for he told me.) The one who told.

rashi.heb:
*ערום יערים הוא.* 
מתנהג הוא בערמה, היום כאן, ולמחר במקום אחר, כדי שלא יודע מקומו:
rashi.eng: *that he deals cunningly.* He acts with cunning; today he is here and tomorrow in another place, so that no one should know where he is.

rashi.heb:
*אל נכון.* 
על דבר מכוון ואמת:
rashi.eng: *with the certainty.* with an exact and true statement.

rashi.heb:
*לפני שאול.* 
שהיה שאול עתיד לילך אחריהם, והם הלכו לפניו לחפש אל נכון:
rashi.eng: *before Saul.* for Saul was destined to go after them, and they went before him, to search (and find out) exactly (where David was).

rashi.heb:
*עוטרים.* 
מקיפים וסובבים מצד אל צד, כעטרה המקפת את הראש:
rashi.eng: *were encircling.* (עטרים, from עטרה, a crown;) i.e., encircling and surrounding from side to side, like a crown which encircles the head.

rashi.heb:
*ומלאך בא אל שאול.* 
מלאך ממש, כדי להציל את דוד:
rashi.eng: *And a messenger came.* (Heb. ‘malach’) a real angel, in order to save David.

notes.687: (sn): The name הַמַּחְלְקוֹת סֶלַע (Sela Hammakhleqoth) probably means “Rock of Divisions” in Hebrew, in the sense that Saul and David parted company there (cf. NAB “Gorge of Divisions”; TEV “Separation Hill”). This etymology assumes that the word derives from the Hebrew root II חלק (khlq, “to divide”; HALOT 322 s.v. II חלק). However, there is another root I חלק, which means “to be smooth or slippery” (HALOT 322 s.v. I חלק). If the word is taken from this root, the expression would mean “Slippery Rock.”

rashi.heb:
*סלע המחלקות.* 
שהיה לבו של שאול חלוק לשתי דעות, אם לשוב להציל את ארצו מיד פלשתים, או לרדוף ולתפוש את דוד, כן תרגמו יונתן:
rashi.eng: *the Rock of the Divisions.* that Saul’s heart was divided by two thoughts, whether to return to save his country from the Philistines, or to pursue David. Thus Jonathan renders.

notes.688: : sn Beginning with 23:29, the verse numbers through 24:22 in the English Bible differ from the verse numbers in the Hebrew text (BHS), with 23:29 ET = 24:1 HT, 24:1 ET = 24:2 HT, 24:2 ET = 24:3 HT, etc., through 24:22 ET = 24:23 HT. With 25:1 the verse numbers in the ET and HT are again the same.

notes.691: (tn): Or “the region of the Rocks of the Mountain Goats,” if this expression is understood as a place name (cf. NASB, NIV, NRSV, TEV, CEV).

notes.692: (tn, Heb): “to cover his feet,” an idiom (euphemism) for relieving oneself (cf. NAB “to ease nature”).

rashi.heb:
*צורי היעלים.* 
סלעי היעלים:
rashi.eng: *צורי היעלים.* the Rocks of the Wild Goats.

rashi.heb:
*להסך את רגליו.* 
להפנות לנקבים גדולים:
rashi.eng: *to cover his feet.* To stool.

notes.694: (tn, Heb): “the heart of David struck him.”

rashi.heb: *ויהי אחרי כן וגו'.*

*ויאמר לאנשיו חלילה.* 
שני מקראות הללו כתובין שלא כסדרן, אלא כיון שהתחיל לדבר בכריתת המעיל, כלה כל דבריו, ואמר שאף בכריתת המעיל נתחרט, ואחר כך חוזר לדברו הראשון, ואומר ; על שאמרו לו אנשיו הנה היום וגו', השיב להם, חלילה לי וגו':
rashi.eng: *And it was afterwards, etc. And he said to his men.* “The Lord forbid…” These two verses are written in reversed order, but since he began to speak of the severing of the coat, he finished all the matter concerning it, and stated that he even regretted the severing of the coat. Afterwards, he returns to his first subject, and states that upon his men’s statement, “Behold, concerning this day, etc.” He retorted to them, “May the Lord forbid it for me, etc.”

rashi.heb:
*וישסע.* 
הבדיל ודחה אותם בדברים:
rashi.eng: *And David stayed.* He separated and held them off with these words.

notes.699: (tn, Heb): “it had pity,” apparently with the understood subject being “my eye,” in accordance with a common expression.

rashi.heb:
*למה תשמע.* 
למה תקבל עלי לשון הרע של דואג:
rashi.eng: *Why should you listen.* Why should you accept Doeg’s slander concerning me?

notes.701: (tn, Heb): “there is not in my hand.”

rashi.heb:
*ואמר להרגך ותחס עליך.* 
הרי כאן חסרים שתי תיבות, ואמר האומר שאהרגך, ותחס נפשי עליך, כמו (שמואל-ב יג לט): ותכל דוד לצאת אל אבשלום, ותכל נפש דוד:
rashi.eng: *and (one) said to kill you, but (my soul) had pity on you.* (lit., and said to kill you, and she had pity on you) Two words are missing here, (to be explained thus): and the sayer said that I should kill you, but my soul had pity on you, similar to “and David longed to go forth to Absalom” (II Sam. 14:2. In our editions, it is 13:39), (meaning): and the soul of David longed.

rashi.heb:
*ואבי ראה.* 
כלומר תן לבך על הדבר, וגם ראה העדות, אשר כנף מעילך בידי, והייתי יכול להרגך:
rashi.eng: *And Father, see!.* i.e., pay attention to the matter, and also see the testimony, for the skirt of your coat is in my hand, and I was able to kill you.

rashi.heb:
*כאשר יאמר משל הקדמוני.* 
משל קדמונו של עולם, התורה, שהיא משלו של הקב"ה:
rashi.eng: *As says the proverb of the ancient one.* the proverb of the Ancient One of the world; i.e., the Torah, which is the proverb of the Holy One Blessed be He.

rashi.heb:
*מרשעים יצא רשע.* 
הקב"ה מזמן לרשע, שנופל ביד רשע כיוצא בו, והיכן אמרה תורה (שמות כא יג): והאלהים אנה לידו כדאיתא במסכת מכות (י ב):
rashi.eng: *“From the wicked one comes forth wickedness”.* The Holy One Blessed be He, destines the wicked to fall into the hand of another wicked man like himself. And where did the Torah say (this)?“And the Lord destined it into his hand” (Ex. 21:13), as it is stated in Tractate Makkoth (10b).

notes.703: (tn): Or “righteous” (so KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV); NAB “you are in the right”; NLT “are a better man than I am.”

rashi.heb:
*ידעתי כי מלוך תמלוך.* 
שרואה אני שהקב"ה מצילך מידי ומדרש אגדה (ילקוט שמעוני רמז קלד): סימן זה מסר לו שמואל, שהקורע מעילו, ימלוך תחתיו:
rashi.eng: *I know that you will reign.* for I see that the Holy One blessed be He saves you from my hand. The Midrash Agadah states: Samuel transmitted this sign to him that the one who tears his coat will reign after him.

notes.706: (tn, Heb): “and David swore an oath to Saul.”

notes.707: (tc): The LXX reads “Maon” here instead of “Paran,” perhaps because the following account of Nabal is said to be in Maon (v. 2). This reading is followed by a number of English versions (e.g., NAB, NIV, NCV, NLT). The MT, however, reads “Paran,” a location which would parallel this portion of David’s life with that of the nation Israel which also spent time in Paran (Num 10:12). Also, the desert of Paran was on the southern border of Judah’s territory and would be the most isolated location for hiding from Saul.

rashi.heb:
*ואיש במעון.* 
שם העיר:
rashi.eng: *in Maon.* the name of the city.

rashi.heb:
*ומעשהו.* 
מקנהו וקנינו:
rashi.eng: *and his possessions.* (lit., his work, or deed.) His cattle and his possessions.

rashi.heb:
*גדול.* 
עשיר:
rashi.eng: *great.* wealthy.

rashi.heb:
*ויהי בגזוז את צאנו בכרמל.* 
ויהי יום אחד בהגיע עת גזוז צאנו בכרמל, ודרכו היה לעשות משתה ויום טוב לגוזזי הצאן:
rashi.eng: *and he was, while shearing his sheep, in Carmel.* And he was one day, when the time of his sheepshearing came around, in Carmel. And his custom was to make a banquet and a festival for the sheepshearers.

notes.709: (sn): The name נָבָל (Nabal) means “foolish” or “senseless” in Hebrew, and as an adjective the word is used especially of persons who have no perception of ethical or religious claims. It is an apt name for this character, who certainly typifies such behavior.
notes.710: (tn, Heb): “good of insight”; KJV “of good understanding”; NAB, NIV, TEV “intelligent”; NRSV “clever.”

rashi.heb:
*והוא כלבי.* 
מבית כלב:
rashi.eng: *a Calebite.* of the house of Caleb.

notes.711: (tn, Heb): “David”; for stylistic reasons the pronoun has been used in the translation.
notes.713: (tn, Heb): “and David said to the young men.”
notes.714: (tn, Heb): “and inquire concerning him in my name in regard to peace.”

notes.715: (tc): The text is difficult here. The MT and most of the early versions support the reading לֶחָי (lekhai, “to life,” or “to the one who lives”). Some of the older English versions (KJV, ASV; cf. NKJV) took the expression to mean “to him who lives (in prosperity),” but this translation requires reading a good deal into the words. While the expression could have the sense of “Long life to you!” (cf. NIV, NJPS) or perhaps “Good luck to you!” this seems somewhat redundant in light of the salutation that follows in the context. The Latin Vulgate has fratribus meis (“to my brothers”), which suggests that Jerome understood the Hebrew word to have an alef that is absent in the MT (i.e., לֶאֱחָי, le’ekhay). Jerome’s plural, however, remains a problem, since in the context David is addressing a single individual, namely Nabal, and not a group. However, it is likely that the Vulgate witnesses to a consonantal Hebrew text that is to be preferred here, especially if the word were to be revocalized as a singular rather than a plural. While it is impossible to be certain about this reading, the present translation essentially follows the Vulgate in reading “my brother” (so also NJB; cf. NAB, RSV, NRSV).

rashi.heb:
*כה לחי.* 
כה יהיה לשנה הבאה, גוזז (כה לחי. כה יהיה לשנה הבאה, מזל חי וקים). (ל"א כה לחי. אמרו על טבחו ונסכו שתראו, כן ראוי לאיש חי, לאיש זריז וחשוב, כמו (שמואל-ב כג כ) בן איש חי רב פעלים, חי ומזורז, בעל מעשים, ע"כ):
rashi.eng: *So.* will he be shearing in the coming year. (So shall be next year living and existing luck.) (Another version is: Say this concerning his meal and his wine, “So is befitting a live man, and active and esteemed man,” like: [II Sam. 23:20] “the son of a live man (kethib) of many heroic deeds.” I.e., alive and active in all his deeds.)

rashi.heb:
*לחי.* 
טוב וקיים:
rashi.eng: *to the living.* good and existing.

rashi.heb:
*ואתה שלום וגו'.* 
כן תהיה לאורך ימים:
rashi.eng: *and peace to you.* So shall it be to the length of days.

rashi.heb:
*לא הכלמנום.* 
אם נצרכו לנו לשום דבר, לא השיבונום ריקם:
rashi.eng: *We did not disgrace them.* If they needed us for anything, we did not send them back empty handed.

rashi.heb:
*ולא נפקד להם.* 
מצאנום כי שומרים היינו להם:
rashi.eng: *neither was anything missing to them..* of your flocks, for we were watching for them.

notes.716: (tc): The translation follows many medieval Hebrew mss in reading בָּאנוּ (ba’nu, “we have come”) rather than the MT’s בָּנוּ (banu, “we have built”).
notes.717: (tn): This refers to the ten servants sent by David.

rashi.heb:
*וימצאו הנערים.* 
שלי, חן בעיניך, בטובה שיגידו לך עבדיך מהם עליהם:
rashi.eng: *and may the youths.* i.e., my youths, find favor in your eyes, for the kindness which your servants will tell concerning them.

rashi.heb:
*כי על יום טוב באנו.* 
על סמך משתה ויום טוב שיש לך, באנו עתה לשאול דבר אחר: ערב ראש השנה היה, וצריכין אנו לסעודת יום טוב:
rashi.eng: *for we have come on a festive day..* Depending upon the banquet and festive day which you have, we have now come to ask. Another explanation is: This was the eve of Rosh Hashanah, (and they said,) “We are in need of a holiday feast.”

rashi.heb:
*וידברו אל נבל ככל הדברים האלה בשם דוד וינוחו.* 
יגעים היו מטורח הדרך, ונזדרזו למצות דוד, ולא נחו עד שדברו אליו, ואחר כך וינוחו ויונתן תרגם: ופסקו, כלומר פסקו מלדבר עוד, עד שישמעו תשובתו:
rashi.eng: *and spoke to Nabal according to all these words, in David’s name, and they rested.* They were weary from the way, yet they were quick to execute David’s command, and did not rest until they spoke to him, and afterwards they rested. Jonathan, however, renders: and they ceased, i.e., they stopped speaking further, until they would hear his reply.

rashi.heb:
*מי דוד.* 
מה הוא חשוב שאתן לו את שלי, הלא מרות המואביה בא:
rashi.eng: *Who is David.* Of what importance is he that I should give him mine? Is he not descended from Ruth the Moabitess?

notes.719: (tn, Heb): “him”; the referent (David) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*ויחגור גם דוד את חרבו.* 
מכאן שמתחילין בדיני נפשות מן הקטנים בדין תחלה (סנהדרין לו א):
rashi.eng: *and David too, girded his sword.* Hence, we derive that in cases involving capital punishment, we commence from the most insignificant in law first.

rashi.heb:
*על הכלים.* 
לשמור אהליהם וכליהם:
rashi.eng: *by the luggage.* to watch their tents and utensils.

rashi.heb:
*אחד מהנערים.* 
שלה:
rashi.eng: *one youth of the youths.* hers.

rashi.heb:
*ויעט בהם.* 
(תרגום:) אפרחינון במלין (ילקוט שמעוני רמז קל"ד, ופירושו הכריחם בדבריו הרעים), לשון עיט (בראשית טו יא):
rashi.eng: *and he drove them away.* (ויעט בהם) With words, he made them fly away. An expression of עיט (a bird) (Gen. 15:11).

notes.721: (tn, Heb): “all the days we walked about with them when we were.”

rashi.heb:
*ולא הכלמנו.* 
לא נכלמנו:
rashi.eng: *and we were not disgraced.* (Heb. הכלמנו ולא. This is synonymous with the usual passive form,) ולא נכלמנו.

notes.722: (tn, Heb): “all his house” (so ASV, NRSV); NAB, NLT “his whole family.”
notes.723: (tn, Heb): “he is a son of worthlessness.”

rashi.heb:
*כי כלתה הרעה.* 
מאת דוד אליו:
rashi.eng: *for the evil has been decided upon.* by David against him.

rashi.heb:
*והוא בן בליעל מדבר אליו.*
